items.title: Patrimeter
items.text: Patrimeter tracks your net worth month by month and shows it as a pyramid: from your main residence, at the base, up to the riskiest investments, at the top. Every month, you enter the balances of your accounts and loans; Patrimeter works out the rest.

items.title: What Patrimeter does
items.text:
• Six-level pyramid: main residence, emergency savings, guaranteed funds, equities, real estate, alternative. Each level shows its net value (assets minus loans) and its share of the total.
  • Monthly update on a single screen; an account without a balance this month keeps its last known balance. The Monthly update menu stands out as long as the month is not entered, and an email reminder is possible.
  • History, at the bottom of the Net worth page: how your net worth and each level change over time, as a chart and a table, and what was put into or taken out of each level since the start of the year.
  • Report to share: the month's net worth on a card that fills the phone screen, with or without the amounts, as a screenshot or as a picture (Mastodon, X, Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram…).
  • Real estate owned in part (joint ownership, couple…), with the loans linked to it.
  • Savings goals: an amount to reach by a date (or months of budget spending); every month, Patrimeter compares your pace with the effort needed and tells whether you are on track, with a projection chart.
  • Trends of the net worth and of the budget over 3, 6 and 12 months, compared with the period before.
  • Household budget: a shared budget paid into the joint account and each adult's share, each person's own expenses and savings, income flows compared with the 50/30/20 rule, read alongside the month's net worth.
  • Family account: each person keeps their account, and a family account brings their data together every month for a view of the family.
  • Carbure: actual spending read from your Carbure instance, next to the planned budget.
  • Recommendations: emergency savings compared with the month's expenses, on a gauge, with an alert below the target.
  • Benchmarks: how your investments are split compared with a balanced allocation, and where your net worth stands among French households and among adults worldwide.
  • On phone and computer alike, in French or English, in a light or dark theme, accessible (contrast, colour blindness, keyboard).
  • API and MCP service for your own tools or an assistant, with the same authentication.

Not financial advice. Patrimeter is a tracking tool: its benchmarks (pyramid, split of the investments, emergency savings, goals) are indicative and are neither financial advice nor investment advice, which is reserved for licensed professionals. Adapt them to your situation.

items.title: Your data stays yours
items.text:
• Self-hosted application: your data does not leave your server.
  • Wealth data encrypted with a key specific to each user, itself protected by their password: neither the server administrator nor a stolen backup can read it.
  • Mandatory two-factor sign-in (authenticator app), passkeys (FIDO2) and security keys available; open sessions visible and signed out from My account.

items.title: Where to start
items.text:
• You are discovering the application: quick start, or Try the demo on the sign-in page of an instance that offers it (trying without an account).
  • You are installing it: on a Linux server (installation) or in a container, with Docker or Podman (container deployment); you are updating it: updating.
  • You already use it: user guide and frequently asked questions. In the application, Documentation (account menu, and sign-in page) leads back here.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: All notable changes to Patrimeter are recorded here (English translation of CHANGELOG.md). Format: Keep a Changelog; numbering: semantic versioning.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Redesigned Challenges page: your two statuses at the top (My level, My profile), a dial of the stars and their split by family of challenges, how far the next level and the next stage are, then the entry streak. Each challenge shows its thresholds from left to right (earned, next, later), what is already done and what is missing for the next star; its rule unfolds. Indicative benchmarks, to adapt to your situation: this is not investment advice.
  • Clearer first start: a "Step 2 of 4" thread at the top of each screen (account, security, recovery key, first accounts), without the misleading "Last step"; "Why two secrets?" tells the backup codes from the recovery key, both of which can be printed; the welcome recommends the questions, then offers the pyramid and folds the three other ways to start; a family account becomes a real choice there.
  • Family members page: each member's status for the month in words ("Up to date", "To update"), their new file dropped on their card, "Remove" folded under "More actions", and the three monthly steps. Under the choice of the view, a line says what it adds up and flags each file to update; "This account" becomes "Family's accounts", and the imported balances are counted "of the month" or "carried over".
  • CI: the test of the Docker Hub image promotion runs in every full pipeline, before any tag, and no longer only at publication time.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Docker Hub publication: the job reads the version of the tested image with Buildah and shares its credentials with Skopeo. In 3.5.0, the registry refused it (403): the 3.5.0 image was not published, 3.6.0 replaces it.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Docker Compose: use the Compose file from this release for the recommended configuration. The HTTP probe applies to the web service; a failed backup or verification is retried after one hour.
  • Linux: reinstalling the same archive preserves data permissions and existing secrets.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Updated the affected Symfony components to 7.4.24, which includes security fixes.
  • The account list decrypts only the latest applicable statement for each displayed balance.
  • An older Docker rebuild can no longer replace a newer build of the same release.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• An account's opening date can no longer be moved beyond the month of an existing statement.
  • Copying a property to an earlier month preserves the initial ownership share for the property and its prorated loan.
  • Viewing challenges or reading the API no longer consumes the star announcement for the next monthly entry.
  • On Linux, the 3.5 updater keeps the last confirmed entry in a verified snapshot outside backup rotation. Rollback rejects a missing or corrupt snapshot before taking the site offline.
  • Monthly reminders can be retried after a mail transport failure.
  • The calendar allows returning to the current month from next month; month and year buttons retain an accessible name that identifies their field.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Compose: set PATRIMETER_IMAGE=docker.io/kartnico1/patrimeter:latest in the Compose .env file.
  • Opt-in publication of releases to Docker Hub, GitHub and GitHub Pages from private GitLab CI.
  • Daily system rebuilds and automatic releases for verified stable Composer security fixes.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Demonstration mode off by default: to keep the "Try the demo" button, add DEMO_MODE=true to the settings (Settings).
  • On Linux, nginx configuration to take again (bank statements and CSV import up to 2 MB, installation wizard); with Docker, nothing to do:
# nginx configuration of the application, that of the new version, then reload of nginx
install -m 0644 /srv/patrimeter/docs/nginx/patrimeter-app.conf /etc/nginx/snippets/patrimeter-app.conf
nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Installation wizard (/installation): on an instance still without any account (demonstration accounts aside), the sign-in page leads to it; it checks the configuration as seen from the browser (HTTPS, address of the site DEFAULT_URI, sending emails, administrator alerts), each point saying what to fix, then creates the first account (address deemed confirmed), signed in and taken to its authenticator app. Only one account can be created this way, even by two visitors at once; afterwards, the page no longer exists. The app:user:create command remains available.
  • Custom indicators: your own totals, pyramid levels and chosen accounts (each account counted once), followed every month as the net worth, with their share of the net worth if you wish; Indicators page (values of the month, change over a month, last twelve months of each), My indicators box on the Net worth page. Encrypted as the other data, they follow the export (format 4, files 1 to 3 still import) and the key rotation (indicators).
  • Reading a bank statement on an account page: the file exported by the bank (OFX or CAMT.053) gives its closing balance and its date, which fill in the statement form, to check then save; nothing is saved nor kept before. QIF or CSV file (without a balance), in a foreign currency or with several accounts: refused with a message that says what to export; XML document without DOCTYPE, nor network access (accounts).
  • "Settings" page in the documentation: changing a setting at any time, on Linux as with Docker (file to edit, service to restart), with examples (demonstration mode, email server) and the main settings, their default value and their effect.

items.title: Changed
items.text: • Fully automatic updates: every Renovate merge request, major versions included, is merged on its own as soon as its pipeline is green; no more dashboard nor approval; the lock file of the PHP dependencies is refreshed every day. doctrine-bundle 3, which requires PHP 8.4, is held until 4.0.0 (docs/ci.md, in French).

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Twig 3.31.1: security fixes published on 23 and 24 November 2026 (automatic escaping, sandbox), found by composer audit.
  • CSV import above 64 KB: nginx refused it (error 413) although the application accepts 1 MB; it now follows the limit of the data import (checked by the deployment job).
A quality release: no change to the screens or the database, nothing to do when updating.

items.title: Added
items.text: • SonarQube analysis in the CI (sonarqube job): bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells, duplication and PHP coverage, against the server's quality gate; the job fails when the gate is not passed. On main and in the full pipelines (or on demand, SONARQUBE=1); server and token in the SONAR_HOST_URL and SONAR_TOKEN variables; SonarScanner pinned by its version and checksum, kept up to date by Renovate (docs/ci.md, in French).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Changelog: versions only, without an "Unreleased" section; changes are written under the version they prepare.
  • Documentation: "Linux" wherever the reader installs Patrimeter (README, home page, requirements, comments of the nginx and php-fpm files); Debian is only named for the container image and the CI, which start from it.
  • Renovate configuration migrated (dependencyDashboard becomes an object), as its dashboard asked; checked by renovate-config-validator --strict.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Dependable load test: k6 keeps the database, the sessions and the cache in memory and turns OPcache on as in production; it measures the application, no longer the stalls of the runner's disk, which made it fail without any code difference (p95 of 0.85 to 1.5 s for a 25 ms median). Same thresholds.
  • Findings of the first SonarQube analysis: regular expressions with a non-linear running time rewritten (thousands separators, address of a Mastodon instance, base64url encoding); label of the hidden username field meant for password managers; the Data page reuses the shared identity confirmation form. The rules that contradict the W3C and the WCAG (scrollable areas reachable from the keyboard, charts described by role="img", focus on the first field of single-form pages) are set aside in sonar-project.properties, each with its reason.

items.title: Removed
items.text:
• "Required Debian packages" page, orphaned and outdated since the archive installation: the requirements are in installation.md, the image's packages in docker/Dockerfile.
  • 3.0.0 proposals (propositions/), delivered: they remain in the git history.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Two supported installations: Docker (compose.yaml) or Linux, from the archive of a version; the installation from git is no longer documented. An installation made from git moves to the archive once: download the archive of this version and its checksum into /tmp, then, as root:
# New patrimeter-update, taken from the archive
ARCHIVE="$(ls /tmp/patrimeter-v*.tar.gz | sort -V | tail -n 1)"
tar -xzf "$ARCHIVE" --strip-components=1 -C /tmp --wildcards '*/docs/update/patrimeter-update.sh'
install -m 0755 /tmp/docs/update/patrimeter-update.sh /usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-update
# Update from the archive; the old folder (with .git) stays in /srv/patrimeter.previous
patrimeter-update "$ARCHIVE"

items.title: Added
items.text: • Property-based tests (fast-check, a development tool): for any amount typed in the monthly entry, the field keeps exactly that amount once formatted, and the level total shows it.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• "Technologies and licenses" page in the documentation: every project used, with its official site, its role and its license.
  • Same titles from one page to another: the page's name in bold, then the month in grey ("Update November 2026" on the three tabs of the monthly update, as "Budget November 2026"); the head buttons in the same format.
  • Months and years picked from a calendar: the month fields (copy of another month, an account's balance, goals) look like the month picker of the page heads ("Oct 2026"); the household's birth years are picked from a calendar of years. Without JavaScript, the text field remains.
  • Saver style offered from the first steps: the "First steps" card asks for it as long as none is chosen.
  • Clearer challenges: score in clear ("1 of 3") and, on each card, the ladder of its stars, from the first at the bottom (earned) to the last at the top, each threshold saying what it asks; total "8 stars of 28" and ladder of the six levels; the saver style is chosen in My profile; the passkey leaves the First steps (five steps), it stays in the Protected account challenge. Always with the notice "Indicative benchmarks, to adapt to your situation: this is not investment advice."
  • Level of the challenges in the net worth box ("★ Level 4: Far-sighted · 15 stars"), with a link to the Challenges page; worked out from the stars already earned, without slowing the page down.
  • No more "My assets" menu: the Accounts and Real estate buttons are at the top of the Net worth page, next to Share; the tax household opens from the Budget page.
  • Monthly update on the right of every menu, always put forward (bold, outlined); red with a dot as long as the month is not entered.
  • Budget page aligned with Savings goals: "Budget" title with the month in grey, Set up tax household and categories button at the top, a single + Enter the budget button when the month has no budget.
  • patrimeter-update installs an archive downloaded by the administrator: checksum checked, database backed up, new version installed next to the old one, migrations, restart; patrimeter-update --rollback brings back the version and the database from before. No more git, Composer or Packagist access on the server.
  • Docker: the database is backed up on every new version, even without a migration (var/backups-before-update, the latest three); compose.yaml no longer builds the image, it pulls it from the registry.
  • Installation and update documentation rewritten: requirements at the top of the page, commented commands ready to copy, without any version number to keep up to date; Release with direct links to the archive, its checksum, compose.yaml and patrimeter.env.example.
  • Security policy: direct link to report a vulnerability (confidential issue), response and fix times, coordinated disclosure.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Delivery archive: files and folders are no longer group-writable (git archive created them as 775 and 664).

items.title: Installation
items.text: • Migrations: a table for the "to refine" balances and a column for the savings rate aimed at; they apply with the usual update. No other address nor variable: nginx and .env.local do not change.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Challenges in the API and the MCP service: GET /api/v1/challenges and the get_challenges tool give the stars, the level, the saver stage and style, the entry streak and each challenge with its thresholds, with the "not investment advice" notice; described in docs/openapi.yaml.
  • Entry streak in the monthly reminder: with the challenges on, the email gives the current streak and what entering the month would bring to it (a new star or the next threshold), with the "not investment advice" notice; worked out from the months entered and the stars earned alone, still without any amount.
  • Simple questions for beginners: a fifth choice at the first sign-in, one question at a time in everyday words, with amounts by ranges, an exact amount or "No"; "Why this question?" gives the level of the pyramid concerned; the last question, optional, chooses the saver style.
  • "To refine" balances: the first balances created by the welcome pages (pyramid, express entry, questions) are marked in the monthly entry until they are saved again (approximate_statements table, without any amount).
  • "Savings rate kept" challenge: the months in a row where the budget plans savings of at least the rate the user chooses themselves on the challenge's card (from 5% to 50%, no rate suggested by default); three more stars (29 in all), also in the API and the MCP.
  • Stars and level on the report: Show my stars adds them to the card and to the shared picture, on request and without any amount (own net worth, challenges on).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• More compact monthly update: an "=" button (or the = key) under each field takes the previous month's balance and moves to the next account; a level whose balances are all entered this month is folded, with its total; the change in net worth from the previous month follows the typing.

  • Updating on a single page (docs/mise-a-jour.en.md): patrimeter-update, checking and rolling back, commands commented and ready to copy; the installation points to it. Shorter README.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• k6 alone on the runner again: it now waits for every job of the test, e2e and security stages (Nuclei, added in 2.25, scanned the application during the measurement and made the p95 threshold fail without any error), and the publication of the documentation waits for it; checked by PerformancePipelineTest.
  • Net worth page as fast as in 2.26: the "First steps" card only measures its six steps, with simple queries, instead of every challenge (goals, safety cushion, streaks); it is not worked out at all once the six steps are done or the card is hidden. The other challenges are measured on the Challenges page and after the monthly entry.

Guided first run and challenges: a new user builds their pyramid in a few minutes, then stars reward their good habits. Indicative benchmarks, to adapt to your situation: this is not investment advice.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Migration: two tables for the challenges and stars; they apply with the usual update.
  • nginx: /defis and /bienvenue join the list of the application's addresses in docs/nginx/patrimeter-app.conf (take the file again; it is part of the container image). Without it, these pages answer 404.
  • Configuration: new optional variable GAMIFICATION (true by default; false removes the challenges from the whole instance).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• First accounts (Net worth page, as long as no account exists): four ways to start. Build my pyramid shows the empty pyramid and its six levels: each level offers its common accounts (current account, Livret A, LDDS, PEA, life insurance…) with today's balance, and takes its colour once filled. Express entry gathers all these accounts on one page. The accounts are created together, opened this month with their balance, all or nothing; a loan is entered by its outstanding principal. The CSV import and the creation account by account remain.
  • Challenges and stars (Challenges menu): eight challenges of good habits (first steps, entry streak with one forgotten month forgiven a year, wealth up to date, safety cushion, no consumer loan, goal under way, budget kept up to date, protected account), up to three stars each; a star earned is never lost. The stars give a level from 1 to 6.
  • Saver profile: a stage computed every month (Discovery, Organized, Protected, Serene, Builder) and an optional style (Ant, Project, Home, Horizon), which only changes the order of the challenges. Neither return, nor share of a level, nor product, nor ranking between users: an architecture test checks it.
  • "First steps" card on the Net worth page: six steps with a link to each, one star each, can be hidden.
  • Stars announced after the monthly entry.
  • Challenges can be turned off by each user (Challenges page or My profile), their stars kept.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Navigation: the Challenges entry follows Monthly update; the bottom bar of a phone adapts to the number of entries.
  • Net worth page without any account: the four ways to start replace "Create a first account"; then, the "First steps" card replaces "Complete your net worth", which stays if the challenges are turned off.
  • Renovate: full image (Node, PHP and Composer already installed), without any GitHub token, every day at 3:00; the CI's Node image is looked up on Docker Hub; Buildah held below 1.44 and endroid/qr-code below 6.1 (PHP 8.4 needed); release notes not fetched.
  • Proposals of 3.0.0 (propositions/3.0.0/): ideas and mockups of the first run, the challenges and the interface.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Test of the demonstration's writes in bursts: it takes the real elapsed time into account (unstable on a slow runner).
  • Renovate: an update of the PHP dependencies also writes THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md again (otherwise its merge request failed on the licenses test).
  • CI: Python stays at 3.14 (Semgrep cannot be installed with 3.15 yet) and OpenSSF Scorecard at 5.6 (5.7 answers 404 on our GitLab); Renovate no longer offers them.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Tax household: the number of adults (one or two) and the number of children (none to 12) are chosen in two lists, and the form only shows the rows of these people, each with their first name and year of birth. The first names of the children are no longer entered separated by commas; a child keeps their budget items when their first name changes, and lowering the number of children removes the last ones of the list. Without JavaScript, all the rows show and only those up to the numbers chosen count.
  • Not financial advice: the README and the documentation home say so; 3.0.0 roadmap: guided first steps (tax household, accounts, properties) and a touch of gamification to support savers.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• CSV import of accounts, loans and properties (Your data, "Create accounts from a CSV file"): one line per account (name, type, opening date; optionally balance and its month, level, nature, share of a property, property and mode of a loan, closing date), added to the existing accounts, all or nothing, with the line at fault in the error message. Model to download in the interface language; spreadsheet files accepted as they are (separator ;, , or tab, UTF-8 or Windows-1252, columns in French or English, DD/MM/YYYY dates, type given by its code or its label). Format documented, with the list of the type codes (documentation, "CSV import").
  • Tax household: the budget speaks of the tax household ("Two adults", without "a couple") and asks for the year of birth of each person; a child who is 16 in the year can have incomes of their own, entered with those of the adults and counted in the household's income (budget flow, export, family account).
  • "My assets" menu, next to Monthly update: Accounts, Real estate, Tax household and categories.
  • Current month of the top bar clickable: it goes back to the current month, on the same page when it shows a month.
  • First steps: the empty Net worth page offers to create an account or a property (or the CSV import), then guides towards what is missing as long as an account and a property do not exist; the Budget part of the monthly update, without a tax household, says so with a single button, Create my tax household.
  • Net worth pyramid: hovering or clicking a level highlights its lines in the other boxes (detail by level, split of the investments, since the start of the year), and a hovered line highlights its level; a click keeps the highlight, Escape removes it.
  • Language of the emails in the profile: French, English, or that of the interface at the time of sending (default); it applies to all the emails, the monthly reminder included.
  • Backup codes and recovery key: a Copy the codes button (one code per line) and a Copy the key button, to paste them into a password manager (shown when the browser allows copying; confirmation announced to screen readers).
  • Renovate every day (schedule RENOVATE=1, job renovate, renovate.json): merge requests updating the PHP libraries and their dependencies (within the constraints of composer.json, lock file refreshed on Mondays), the Node tools, the images and tools of the CI (Composer, k6, Nuclei, OpenSSF Scorecard, Docker Compose, Semgrep, Zensical, Renovate itself) and the Debian image of the container. Versions published for at least 14 days, a known flaw without waiting; major versions after approval on the dependency dashboard; SHA-256 checksums and tag of the CI image recomputed by ci/renovate-post-upgrade.sh. This pipeline only runs Renovate (RenovatePipelineTest).
  • 3.0.0 roadmap: family mode to rework.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Security alerts by email: after an action that may have shut the user out of the account (password changed or reset, authenticator app replaced, account deleted), the email no longer advises to change the password from My account, a dead end for someone who can no longer sign in: it asks to tell the server administrator.
  • Without any account, the Net worth and Monthly update pages stay on the current month (no arrows nor selector), the one where the first accounts are created.
  • Goals: the "+ Set a goal" button, when no goal exists, becomes "View your goals".
  • Without any account, the monthly update no longer offers to copy the balances of another month.
  • Months written with a capital in French when they stand alone (top bar, titles, columns, calendar), as in English; within a sentence, the French lower case stays.
  • CSV import: the model is downloaded with a button, shown before the form.
  • Logo of the header and of the report aligned with the site icon (favicon): the same triangle with a light tip, in the same colours, the report image included.

items.title: Removed
items.text: • Home-made Monday dependency bot (job dependency-update, ci/update-dependencies.sh, tools/npm-update.mjs, tools/dependency-mr.mjs): Renovate replaces it.

items.title: Installation
items.text: • A migration (language of the emails): applied by the usual update. On the GitLab project: create the daily Renovate schedule (Build > Pipeline schedules, branch main, 0 5 * * *, variable RENOVATE = 1, docs/ci.md, in French); the existing DEPENDENCY_BOT_TOKEN token is used by Renovate; GITHUB_COM_TOKEN (GitHub token without rights) is optional.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Carbure synchronisation: the address of the MCP service that Carbure shows (https://…/api/mcp) was kept as is, and Patrimeter called …/api/mcp/api/mcp, to which Carbure answers 404: linking failed, with a message blaming the token. This address is now brought back to that of the instance, and a link already saved this way works without entering anything again. The message now tells a refused token (401, 403) apart from an address without a Carbure MCP service (404, 405); a hint under the field says that both addresses will do.

items.title: Added
items.text: • AI agents: a Copy button next to the address of the MCP service and that of the REST API, in "Connect an AI agent" (shown when the browser allows copying; "Copied" confirmation, announced to screen readers).

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Budget, "Budget trends" box on a phone: the column headings ran over each other; they become "Expenses" and "Savings" (the introduction already says it is an average per month), and a column heading too long now wraps instead of running over its neighbour.
Markdown checks of the documentation and Nuclei scan, of the application in the CI and of the deployed instance.

items.title: Installation
items.text: • CI (developers): PRODUCTION_URL (.gitlab-ci.yml) gives the address of the deployed instance that nuclei-production scans on Mondays; empty: no scan. Nothing changes for an installation.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Nuclei in the CI (ProjectDiscovery, pinned version and checksum, CI tool only): nuclei job on the application started in the pipeline (HTTP templates of the day, "low" severity and up, without the intrusive templates), report sent to the security gate; nuclei-production job on the deployed instance, without account and at a reduced rate, on Mondays and on demand (PRODUCTION_SCAN=1), which fails on a High or Critical finding without ever blocking a release (CI, in French).
  • Markdown checked in the fast pipeline: markdownlint (.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc, tuned for Zensical) on the repository, docs/ and documentation/; the anchors of the links between pages of the site checked with Zensical's rule (DocumentationLinksTest).

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Nested lists of the CHANGELOG and of the Accessibility page: indented by 4 spaces, they finally show nested in the documentation site.

items.title: Security
items.text: • Development tools: re2js forced to 2.9.1 (overrides of package.json) for advisory GHSA-gg6h-894w-4m9c of markdownlint; the picomatch advisory without a fix stays excluded until 1 December, markdownlint-cli2 included.
User list for the administrator; registrations never confirmed deleted after 24 hours.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• app:user:list: users of the instance (address, creation, address confirmation, second factor, number of accounts, last sign-in) and totals, without decrypting anything; --json for a script (installation, § 6).
  • Unconfirmed registrations deleted: the hourly scheduled task erases a registration never confirmed 24 hours after the last link sent (the address becomes free again); never an account holding accounts, nor a demo account, nor an account without address.

items.title: Security
items.text: • Development tools: advisory GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (picomatch, ReDoS), without a fixed version so far, is excluded from the gate until 1 December, with its justification (security/exclusions.json): it only affects Stylelint, Vitest and Vite, never production.
Goals view redesigned; recognizable API tokens, checked origins of the MCP service, trusted browsers.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Optional: MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, origins of web pages allowed to call the MCP service besides the site (separated by commas without spaces; empty by default) (installation, § 3). Nothing to do for a client outside a browser (Claude Code, script).
  • Database: a migration adds the trusted_browsers table (run by the update).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Trusted browsers: on the code screen, "Trust this browser for 30 days"; the next sign-ins on this browser only ask for the password. Listed in My account > Sign-in and security, removed one by one or all together; a new password or signing out the other sessions removes them too; sign-in without code recorded in the log.
  • MCP service origins: a request whose Origin header is neither the site nor an origin of MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS gets 403, even before the firewall (MCP specification, DNS rebinding).

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Goals view: progress ring with a "where you should stand" mark, status pill, key figures as tiles (current amount, target, effort needed, pace observed), interactive projection chart (shaded area, bubble of the amounts on hover, axis zoomed on the data, target as a thin line); a sentence under the chart repeats the figures.
  • Recognizable API tokens: patrimeter_ followed by 24 hexadecimal characters, _ and 43 characters; a secret detector spots a token published by mistake (patrimeter-api-token rule of .gitleaks.toml). The pm1.… tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.

Simpler goal form (lists, fields according to the choices, start month), steadier guided tour, hour and sender of the monthly reminder; faster CI (ready-made image, reduced tag pipeline).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Start month of a goal: this month by default, or a past month for a goal already under way; the value measured in that month is the starting point (computed again if the start month or what the goal measures changes).
  • Monthly reminder: it leaves on the chosen day from 9:00 (the instance's time), never at night any more; the section of "My account" gives the hour and the sender's address (MAIL_FROM, already visible in every email).

items.title: Changed
items.text:

  • Guided tour: the "Previous" button is always there (greyed out at the first step), so "Next" no longer moves from one step to the next.
  • CI (developers): the PHP jobs start from a ready-made image (PHP 8.3 to 8.5 from Surý, pcov, Composer), built by the ci-php-image job only when what makes it up changes, and on Mondays; the pipeline of a tag no longer replays the checks already passed on main (.not-tag rule): it builds, analyses and publishes the release (CI, in French). Every pipeline checks the syntax and runs all the PHPUnit suites on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 (8.4 now linted too), a rule locked by PhpVersionsCiTest.

items.title: Added
items.text:

  • Savings planned in the budget compared with the effort needed, for the savings items tied to the goal's accounts.
  • Projection chart of each goal: reached, planned trajectory and projection at the current pace, told apart by the style of the line and described in text.

items.title: Added
items.text:

Every month, the effort still needed is compared with the pace of the last six months: Reached, Ahead, On track, To watch, Behind or Too early to tell, with what is missing each month and the month the goal would be reached at this pace; status of the last months.

A banner reminds when it is deleted: after 2 hours, or as soon as you sign out, with all its data.

Open sessions visible and signed out, passkeys (FIDO2), encrypted copy of the backups off the server and monthly test restore, optional check of the latest version, third-party licenses, documented workflow; Monday rebuild of the image fixed.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Migration: new table of the open sessions; it applies with the usual update.
  • Debian server: patrimeter-update installs and enables the monthly test restore (patrimeter-restore-check.timer). From the archive, install it as in § 1 of the backup page.
  • Optional: encrypted copy of the backups off the server (apt-get install age, PATRIMETER_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENTS and PATRIMETER_BACKUP_COPY variables, backup, § 2); daily check of the latest version (UPDATE_CHECK_URL, UPDATE_CHECK_TOKEN, monitoring). Without them, nothing changes.
  • Container: the image contains age; the same optional variables go into patrimeter.env.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Open sessions (My account > Sign-in and security): a box lists, like the sign-in log, every signed-in device (sign-in, last activity, IP address, browser), the current session marked. Once the identity is confirmed, Sign out closes another session, Sign out my other sessions closes them all except yours; the device goes back to the sign-in page at its next request.
  • "Update my household" link in the budget entry, next to adding an item and an account.
  • Encrypted copy of the backups off the server: the archive encrypted with age for public keys only, then handed to a copy command of your choice (rsync, rclone…); a copy in clear is refused, a missed copy fails the backup and warns the administrator.
  • Monthly test restore of the latest archive (patrimeter-restore --check-latest), email alert on failure; in the container, after each backup.
  • Daily check of the latest version, disabled by default: a more recent version is reported by email to the administrator, by /sante and by a metric.
  • Third-party licenses: THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md lists the third-party code shipped (Composer dependencies, Chart.js) and its license, kept up to date by a test.
  • Documented workflow (docs/developpement.md, in French): branches, merge requests, pipelines and their variables, publishing a version, Release and image, to follow by hand.
  • Quality badges in the README.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Passkeys: the interface says "passkey (FIDO2)" everywhere; in "Passkeys (FIDO2) and security keys", the reminder to confirm your identity before adding or changing a device is highlighted.
  • Dependencies of 16/11 (Doctrine DBAL 4.6, PHPUnit 12.5.44, Psalm 7.7…).
  • Weekly dependency merge request written in English, like the rest of the project.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Monday image: rebuilding the latest version failed since Dockerfile moved into docker/ (checked-out version that keeps it at the root).
  • Theme and language preferences: their one-year lifetime counts in real time; they no longer depend on the application's clock.
  • Documentation: number of account types, remaining mentions of sign-in with an external account.

Hardening and tidying: nginx allowlist and limits on the sign-in forms, self-updating container, Docker files moved to docker/, roadmap by version; report as a picture to share on social networks; next month shown on the Net worth page.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Debian server, nginx: two files to take again (installation, § 8): docs/nginx/patrimeter-limits.conf, new, to copy into /etc/nginx/conf.d/, and docs/nginx/patrimeter-app.conf, to copy again into /etc/nginx/snippets/; then nginx -t and systemctl reload nginx. Without the first one, nginx refuses the second.
  • Container: Dockerfile and compose.yaml are now in docker/, with the patrimeter.env.example template; the docker compose commands are run from that folder, where patrimeter.env also goes (container). The image built by the CI keeps its address.
  • Boolean variables (REGISTRATION_ENABLED, API_ENABLED, MCP_ENABLED, SHOW_VERSION): documented with true and false; 1 and 0 are still accepted.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Report as a picture, to share: on a phone, the report card fills the whole screen; below it, Patrimeter turns it into a picture (1080 × 1350 PNG, in the browser) to share through the phone's share sheet, save, or post on Mastodon (any server), X (Twitter), Facebook, WhatsApp or Instagram. With amounts, a warning reminds that a posted picture makes them public. Patrimeter sends nothing.
  • nginx allowlist: only the application's addresses reach PHP, any other gets a 404 error from nginx; HTTP methods limited to GET, HEAD and POST outside the API and the MCP; sign-in, registration, forgotten password and unlock forms limited to 30 submissions per minute and per address (429 error beyond). A test checks that every route of the application is covered.
  • Global registration cap: 30 per hour, all addresses together, on top of the per-address limit; a script that changes address no longer creates accounts in bulk.
  • Self-updating container: before applying the migrations of a new version, the app container backs up the database in the data volume (var/backups-before-migration, latest three); scheduler and backup wait until app has prepared the new version.
  • Roadmap (ROADMAP.md) by version, the structural changes in 3.0.0; project quality badges on GitLab.

items.title: Fixed

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Second home: new property type, in the Real estate level of the pyramid; its loans have their own type, second home mortgage.
  • Tangible assets in the Alternative level: silver and other precious metals (platinum, palladium), jewellery, watches, works of art and collectibles, wines and spirits, car, motorbike; gold keeps its type, now "Gold".
  • Next month: the net worth update, the budget entry and the Budget page go up to the following month, to prepare its balances or its budget in advance; the calendar still marks the current month.

Three-entry navigation, all the settings in My account, monthly update in two parts, history at the bottom of the Net worth page, savings of the year, password strength in real time, account deletion.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Since the start of the year: under the source of the investment split, what was put into or taken out of each level of the pyramid since the end of December (or January), and for the net worth: an overview of the savings of the year, gains and repayments included (net worth).

  • Monthly update in two parts: Net worth (balances of the accounts) and Budget, for the same month.
  • Password strength in real time: at registration, password change, password reset and when choosing an unlock passphrase, a bar and a label (from Very weak to Very strong) estimate the strength the way the server does, and each requirement (length, without the email address, unpredictable enough, same confirmation) is ticked or crossed as you type.

items.title: Changed
items.text:

Account menu and My account page in tabs, AI agents tab, update from git in one command, footer with copyright and license, hideable version.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Update from git with a script, patrimeter-update [main | vX.Y.Z], like the backup: it checks, backs up, sets up the new code then lets the script of the new version run its steps, and records the previous commit for rolling back. The first time, run it from main (updating).
  • New optional variable SHOW_VERSION: 0 hides the version at the bottom of the pages (shown by default).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Hideable version: SHOW_VERSION=0 hides the Patrimeter version at the bottom of the pages, sign-in page included; it is still shown by default (installation § 3).
  • Account menu: the My account button opens a menu with My profile, AI agents (if the API or the MCP is enabled) and Sign out.
  • My account page in tabs: Profile, Sign-in and security, AI agents (addresses of the MCP service and of the API, tokens and applications) and Sign-in log.
  • Footer: copyright, license (free software under the MIT license) and link to the Patrimeter project, before the version.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
