  • Project: commits, merge requests, TODO.md and code comments are now written in English, for an international project; the interface and the documentation stay in French and English.
Family account, dashboard recommendations, budget compared with net worth in charts, actual spending read from Carbure; API and MCP disabled by default.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• REST API and MCP service disabled by default: if you use them, add API_ENABLED=1 and/or MCP_ENABLED=1 to .env.local (or to the container's environment file) before updating (api.en.md).
  • New optional variable CARBURE_ALLOWED_HOSTS: hosts of the Carbure instances that users can link (empty: all, local network included); set it on an instance open to the public.
  • nginx configuration changed: importing a member's file into a family account (/famille/membres) accepts 2 MB, like the data import. From git or from the CI archive, copy docs/nginx/patrimeter-app.conf again into /etc/nginx/snippets/ and reload nginx (installation § 8); the container image already includes it.
  • Two migrations create the tables of family account members and of Carbure links; the update procedure applies it, like the container image when it starts. From git, do not forget php bin/console asset-map:compile. Container image: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Family account: each of the two members of a couple keeps their own account and exports its data every month; a third account imports them (Family members page), each new import replacing the previous one:
    • the dashboard, the history, the report and the budget show the whole family, one member or this account; the choice is kept from one page to the next;
    • the family adds everything up, each person having entered their share of what is shared (half of the joint account, share of the house, share of the expenses); the family budget makes each member an adult, brings together children with the same first name and is read-only;
    • the imported file is validated like an ordinary import, then kept encrypted with the family account's key.

  • Recommendations on the dashboard, to the right of how investments are split: emergency savings compared with the month's budget expenses on a gauge in months of expenses, with a finding (Alert below one month, Warning below the target with the missing amount, Good, or Note above twice the target); pyramid rules: base first, negative level, largest gap with the allocation benchmark.

  • Carbure (github.com/ltoinel/Carbure, self-hosted bank spending tracker): each user links their own instance (Budget → Carbure: address and API token); their expense categories are mapped to the budget's (by name, then by hand), and the budget page shows the planned amount, the month's actual spending and the gap. Read-only through Carbure's MCP server, without a new dependency; encrypted token; a single path called, without redirects, with bounded delay, size and number of calls.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• REST API and MCP service disabled by default, each enabled by its variable (API_ENABLED, MCP_ENABLED), as in Carbure: a disabled service answers 404 on all its addresses; the OAuth server and personal tokens only exist if one of the two is enabled.
  • Budget, "With your net worth" section: key figures (net worth and its change, emergency savings, expenses of the month), the same gauge as the dashboard, "planned" and "change in balance" bars for each savings payment, with their finding.
  • Data export: reading a file is shared by the ordinary import and a member's import.
  • TODO: technical ideas taken from Carbure.
Monthly household budget, read alongside the net worth of the same month.

items.title: Installation
items.text: • Ordinary update (docs/mise-a-jour.en.md): a migration creates the budget tables; the update procedure applies it, as does the container image when it starts. No variable or configuration to change. From git, do not forget php bin/console asset-map:compile. Container image: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Monthly household budget (Budget menu), modelled on a couple's spreadsheet:
    • household of one or two adults and their children; suggested categories and items, to rename, add to or delete, each category placed in a group of the 50/30/20 rule (needs, wants, savings) and paid from the joint account or by one adult;
    • entry of a month's amounts (each adult's net income, the amount of each item), carried over to the following months until the next change; totals worked out as you type;
    • joint account: total of the shared budget, split in proportion to income or by a fixed share; each adult's own expenses and savings, and what they have left;
    • income flows as a chart (Sankey diagram drawn by the server, with no new library), 50/30/20 rule, savings rate, cost of each child;
    • read alongside the net worth of the same month: emergency savings in months of expenses against a target, savings payments next to the change in the balance of the linked accounts, net worth;
    • everything is encrypted with the user's key, and the budget routes are crawled by the isolation robot.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Data export: format version 2, with the household budget; a version 1 file can still be imported. The characters <, >, &, ' and " are escaped in the file.
  • Navigation: six entries; short labels on medium-width screens, so that they fit on one line.
  • Back to the original display for the monthly update, accounts, properties and the budget: one card per section, bold headings, the usual font (no more fixed-width figures or small caps), boxed fields, carried-over balance with a dashed border on an amber background. The features remain: totals as you type, statuses, change since the previous month, keyboard shortcuts. The new layout is postponed to version 3.
Documentation and README in English, new layout for accounts and properties, amounts read in the language of the page, up-to-date versions and code quality review.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Ordinary update (docs/mise-a-jour.en.md): no variable, configuration or migration to change. From git, do not forget php bin/console asset-map:compile: without it, the old layout of the accounts remains. Container image: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d.
  • Online documentation: new addresses, …/patrimeter/fr/ and …/patrimeter/en/; the old ones lead to the French site.

items.title: Added
items.text: • Documentation and README in English: the online documentation exists in French and in English, as two twin sites with the same paths (…/patrimeter/fr/ and …/patrimeter/en/), whose language selector stays on the same page; the root opens the browser's language and the old addresses lead to the French site. User and operations pages, API reference (English OpenAPI description, docs/openapi.en.yaml), CHANGELOG and security policy translated (README.en.md, CHANGELOG.en.md, SECURITY.en.md, docs/*.en.md); screenshots taken in each language. The technical pages about developing Patrimeter (architecture, CI…) remain in French. A test checks that every page has its translation, with the same sections, code blocks and screenshots, and that the commands run by the CI are identical in both languages.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• New layout for accounts and properties, in the style of the monthly update:
    • list of accounts as one table per level (status entered or carried over, balance for the month in tabular figures, loans marked "owed");
    • account page with its summary (type, level, nature, opening), its statements and its shares as tables;
    • properties as tables, loans detailed and net value in the footer;
    • status of a balance as a shared template and shared table styles (.sheet, .ledger); the fields of a form row no longer stretch to the height of their neighbour.
  • Up-to-date versions:
    • CI on Debian 13 (like the container image and the checked installation), Node 24 (LTS) and Python 3.14;
    • JavaScript tools: Vitest 5 and jsdom 30;
    • doctrine/doctrine-bundle 2.19.4;
    • the other tools and images were already at their latest version published at least two weeks ago; more recent versions will come through the Monday merge request.
  • Documentation built in strict mode (a broken link or anchor fails the build); command variables in English ($TOKEN, $PASSWORD, NEW_PHP), like the rest of the code; update guide: the installed version is read in VERSION or at the bottom of the page.
  • Code quality: account nature and loan mode as enumerations (Nature, LoanMode) instead of strings; typed class constants (PHP 8.3), enforced by a test; mutation testing extended to the encryption code (MSI of 94%); #[\Override] exemption limited to the published migrations.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Amounts on an English page: "1,000" (one thousand, English style) was refused as an amount with three decimals. Amounts are now read in the language of the page: comma as the thousands separator in English ("1,000"), dot in French ("1.000"); the other reading of the same text, with three decimals, is still refused. Same rule for the totals worked out as you type.
  • Password-too-short message left in French on English pages (registration, forgotten password, password change): built before being translated, it escaped the translator. A test now refuses a computed constraint message; every page, rendered in English, has been reviewed.
  • Registration: the page after sending the form said "If the address can be registered, a message has just been sent to it", an obscure wording. It now shows the address entered and explains both cases: confirmation link for a new registration, simple notice if the address already has an account. The page stays the same in both cases: it still does not reveal who is registered.
Version shown on every page, and entering past months from a later month.

items.title: Installation
items.text: • Ordinary update (docs/mise-a-jour.en.md): no variable, configuration or migration to change. From git, do not forget php bin/console asset-map:compile. Container image: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Version shown at the bottom of every page, sign-in page included ("Patrimeter, version X.Y.Z"). It comes from the VERSION file, present in every installation (git, archive, image) and kept in line with the CHANGELOG by a test.
  • Entering a past month from a later month: on a month without any open account, the page offers to copy the balances of a later month (the current month by default); the copy also includes the accounts opened after the month being entered, and saving moves their opening date back to the 1st of that month (in the same transaction as the balances). Example: Patrimeter started in November, October is filled in by copying November.

Container deployment (Docker, Docker Compose, Podman), new monthly update, report to share as a screenshot, OpenAPI description of the API, copying an entry, month calendar and type lists you can type into.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• Ordinary update (docs/mise-a-jour.en.md): no variable, configuration or migration to change. From git, do not forget php bin/console asset-map:compile: without it, the old layout remains.
  • New: container deployment, described in docs/docker.en.md.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Monday pipeline (docs/ci.md, in French), on top of the security scans:
    • the image of the latest version is rebuilt with the Debian and PHP packages of the day, started, analysed by Trivy and, if everything passes, published again as vX.Y.Z, latest and vX.Y.Z-YYYYMMDD: containers get the security fixes with docker compose pull, without waiting for a version;
    • the dependencies (Composer, Node tools) are updated, checked by make lint cs stan psalm test audit js and proposed in a merge request, as a draft if a check fails. Token to create once: DEPENDENCY_BOT_TOKEN.
  • CI quality checks:
    • JavaScript and CSS: ESLint ("flat" configuration) and Prettier, Stylelint;
    • JavaScript unit tests with Vitest;
    • mutation testing of the business code with Infection (MSI of at least 92%);
    • accessibility of every page with axe-core in Playwright (WCAG 2.2 AA, light and dark themes);
    • migrations run on a new database, and checked up to date (doctrine:migrations:up-to-date);
    • lint:yaml extended to the translations and the OpenAPI description;
    • container: hadolint at the strictest threshold, docker compose config, image built early in the pipeline, smoke test of the started container, Trivy on the built image.
  • OpenAPI 3.1 description of the REST API (docs/openapi.en.yaml): each operation, its parameters, its request bodies, its responses (errors included) and its schemas. Published in the online documentation: "API reference" page, generated from the description at every build, and a file to import into a client or a code generator. A test checks that it covers exactly the API routes and that the actual responses follow its schemas.
  • Container deployment, with Docker and Docker Compose or Podman (docs/docker.en.md): Dockerfile (Debian 13 and PHP 8.5 from the Surý repository, the recommended versions; nginx and php-fpm, same settings as a server) and compose.yaml (application, scheduled tasks, daily backup; data and backup volumes). Migrations applied at start, patrimeter-console console, image checked when it is built. The CI builds the image with Buildah, without a daemon or privileged mode (container-image job), and publishes it in the project registry for every version: docker pull registry.example.org/kartzone/patrimeter:v2.5.0.
  • Report to share: Share, on the dashboard, opens a card of the month the size of a phone screen (net worth, change over 1 month and 1 year, pyramid, assets and liabilities), without menus, to capture and send as a picture (WhatsApp, Signal, text message, email…). Only the levels appear, never the name of an account; Hide amounts only keeps the percentages. Nothing is published: the page remains private.
  • Copying an entry: on the monthly update page, "Copy balances from another month" fills the form with the balances of the chosen month (entered or carried over), to check and then save; nothing is saved before. Handy to fill in a past year from a month already entered.
  • Calendar for month fields (statement of an account, share of a property, copying an entry): a button opens the year + month grid of the month selector; typing YYYY-MM with the keyboard remains possible.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Recommended versions: Debian 13 and PHP 8.5. The published container image is built with them, and the documented installation is checked by the CI on them (PHP 8.3 to 8.5 remain supported). The documentation no longer names a Debian version: the PHP repository is configured with the code name read from the system, the same procedure works for any version. The part specific to LXC containers is removed.
  • New layout for the monthly update: one slim table per level (account, status, previous month's balance, amount), "Level net" and the month's net worth worked out again as you type (property shares included), discreet difference with the previous month under a changed amount, "X/N entered" counter with its mini progress bar. Amounts in tabular figures, aligned on the decimal separator, with "€" everywhere; loans marked "owed", their "−" next to the amount (accepted when saving, with or without the sign). Keyboard: Enter moves to the next field without sending the form, Shift+Enter to the previous one, Esc restores the suggested amount. Shortcuts and reminders folded behind a "?" help. Documentation and screenshots updated (new screenshot of the help, in the dark theme).
  • Account and property types: list you can type into: you type directly in the "Type" field and the list only keeps the types that contain the text (ignoring case and accents), groups kept; mouse, arrows, Enter, Esc. Replaces the separate "Filter" field; without JavaScript, the full list remains.
  • Online documentation: Patrimeter's favicon replaces Zensical's; every "§" reference is a link to the section it refers to, and the accented anchors, ignored by Zensical, are fixed.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Up-to-date container image (found by Trivy on the image): the packages of the Debian base image, pinned by its digest, did not receive their security fixes (zlib); every build now applies them. A version is only published in the registry once the smoke test and the security gate have passed.
  • Accessibility (found by axe-core): the accessible name of the month selector includes the text shown (WCAG 2.5.3), and the tables that scroll sideways (sign-in log, monthly values) can be reached with the keyboard.
  • The application's JavaScript no longer adds its functions to window.
  • "My account" page in English: the "Sign in" line of the profile stayed in French. The text was chosen before being translated, which hid it from the translation check; a test now refuses this construction.
Investment split benchmark, language menu, rankings side by side, property type filter, English translations reviewed and update guide completed.

items.title: Installation
items.text: • Ordinary update (docs/mise-a-jour.en.md): no variable or configuration to change. From git, do not forget php bin/console asset-map:compile: without it, the old layout remains.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Investment split benchmark, under the pyramid: share of each level in your investments (guaranteed funds, equities, real estate, alternative), next to the "balanced" allocation of Avenue des Investisseurs (45 / 25 / 25 / 5%), with its source; only a guide, excluding the main residence and emergency savings.
  • Property type filter when creating a property, as for accounts: ignoring case and accents.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Language selector: the button shows the current language (globe, FR or EN) and opens a Français / English menu, the current language ticked; works without JavaScript, closes when clicking elsewhere or with Esc.
  • Rankings side by side: position among French households and among adults worldwide, one card each on the same row, under the pyramid and the details by level (one under the other on a phone).
  • English translations reviewed: more natural sign-in and entry vocabulary ("Sign in", "Monthly update", "balances"), "fonds euros" translated as "guaranteed funds", wording of the rankings.

  • Update guide completed: compiling the assets among the steps, "Common problems" section (display still old, git pull refused, error 500, failed migration). User documentation: benchmarks, language, frequently asked questions.

  • Tidier repository: merged branches deleted (repository and local copies), source branch deleted by default when a merge request is merged; rule for branches and tags in docs/ci.md.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: • Simultaneous entries refused ("database is locked") when a write kept the database for more than 5 s on a slow disk: SQLite now waits up to 15 s for a lock before giving up.

items.title: Removed
items.text:
• docs/plan.md, historical plan of v2 (no longer kept up to date, kept in the git history).
  • "Skip to content" link at the top of the pages: the Patrimeter logo in the header leads back to the dashboard, and the marked-up areas (header, navigation, content) are enough for screen readers.
Interface in English, position among adults worldwide, accessibility, accounts and properties separated, "My account" page and update guide.

items.title: Installation
items.text: • Ordinary update (docs/mise-a-jour.en.md): no variable, nor nginx or php-fpm configuration to change. The new dependency (symfony/translation) is installed by Composer, or already included in the version's archive.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Interface in English: browser language by default (French otherwise), FR / EN button next to the theme button (choice kept in a cookie). Pages, messages, emails, amounts (€1,234.56), dates and months translated; Symfony's Translation component, translations/*.en.yaml catalogues, translation completeness test. The documentation, the API and the console remain in French.
  • Position among adults worldwide, under the position among French households: share of adults whose net worth is lower, scale graduated at the band thresholds, thresholds in euros and dollars, source (UBS, Global Wealth Report 2026, net worth per adult at the end of 2025, converted at the ECB rate of 31/12/2025).
  • Step-by-step update guide (docs/mise-a-jour.en.md): installed version, what to read in the CHANGELOG, installing a specific version, verification, rollback. The CI archive contains a RELEASE file (name of the archive and commit).
  • Account type filter when creating an account: only keeps the types that contain the text typed, ignoring case and accents; full list without JavaScript.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA targeted, Accessibility page of the documentation):
    • level colours reviewed to remain distinct for colour-blind people (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) and readable under white text (light) or dark text (dark theme, new shades);
    • a pattern specific to each level in the history chart, on top of its colour;
    • input field borders and "carried over" text with enough contrast;
    • "Skip to content" link;
    • errors announced immediately to screen readers;
    • automatic test of the contrasts and of the difference between colours for colour-blind people, in both themes.
  • Accounts and properties separated: one menu each ("Properties" in the navigation). Properties (main residence, rental, SCPI, SCI…) are only created from Real estate, with their share and their loans: the account form no longer offers their types and refuses an account that would become a property (Residence or Real estate level, asset). An existing property can still be changed.
  • "My account" page in place of the Security page (same address, /securite): the user's profile first, then security and data; link with a profile icon, above "Sign out".

items.title: Added
items.text: • Position among French households, under the pyramid: share of households whose net worth is lower, decile, graduated scale, thresholds and source (Insee, Histoire de vie et Patrimoine survey 2023-2024, net worth in early 2024). Calculated locally, by interpolation between the published thresholds.
Monitoring, data export and import, server key rotation, CSP violation reports, rate limited per token, online user documentation, Symfony and PHP best practices.

items.title: Installation
items.text: • To update a server already installed: copy the php-fpm pool again (docs/php-fpm/patrimeter.conf, upload of the import file) and docs/nginx/patrimeter-app.conf (import address up to 2 MB), then nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx; the var/uploads folder is created by the update.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• User documentation published by GitLab Pages (Zensical): quick start, screen-by-screen guide with screenshots taken from the application at every main pipeline, installation and operations taken from docs/ without a copy to maintain.
  • Data export and import (Your data page, from Security): versioned JSON file, to move from one Patrimeter instance to another; all-or-nothing import into an empty account (docs/export.en.md).
  • Monitoring: /sante (JSON status, 503 if the database does not answer) and /sante/metriques (Prometheus format, also read by the OpenTelemetry Collector): database, age of the last backup and of the scheduled tasks, free space (docs/supervision.en.md).
  • CSP violation reports logged in var/log/csp-*.log (report-uri, report-to).
  • Rate limited per token on the API and MCP: 120 requests in a row, then one per second (429).
  • Rotating AUTH_SECRET_KEY without resetting the users: AUTH_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS and app:auth-secrets:rotate (installation § 12.5).
  • Security pipeline every Monday (SECURITY_SCAN=1), even without new code; main protected.
  • List of upcoming improvements: TODO.md.
  • Procedure to publish a version (git tag, GitLab Release): docs/ci.md.
  • docs/choix-techniques.md: all the technical building blocks, the alternatives considered and the reason for each choice.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• OPcache tuned as Symfony recommends (docs/php-fpm/patrimeter-opcache.ini, to copy to /etc/php/<version>/fpm/conf.d/90-patrimeter.ini, installation § 7): 256 MB, file timestamps not checked. After any change to the code outside the update procedures, restart php-fpm. No preloading: with the pool's disable_functions list, it distorted function calls (error 500 found by the deployment job, fixed before any installation).
  • Service container compiled into a single file; locale limited to French.
  • API controllers on AbstractController, like the others.
  • PHP 8.3 best practices: #[\Override] on every overridden method, required by PHPStan and Psalm; #[\SensitiveParameter] on the tokens, codes and secrets that did not have it.
  • Services configured by attributes next to the code (#[AsMiddleware], #[AsAlias], #[Autowire]).
  • Deprecations: PHPUnit reports those of Symfony and Doctrine at their caller (Symfony's recipe), Doctrine's are enabled in tests; the CI refuses the deprecations reported when compiling the container (tools/container-deprecations.sh).
  • Status of Symfony best practices, deliberate deviations included: docs/architecture.md.
  • .gitattributes: LF line endings enforced.
  • PHP-CS-Fixer 3.95.30, Psalm 7.2.
  • No more mention of PHP 8.2 in the repository (documentation, plan, php-fpm pool); the PHP 8.3 polyfill is no longer installed, useless since PHP 8.3 is the minimum (as Symfony's skeleton does).

items.title: Removed
items.text: • settings table, inherited from v1 and unused since the move to multiple users (migration Version20261110140000, reversible); config/preload.php, OPcache preloading not being used.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Changing the PHP version (installation § 12.4): the new php-fpm, started when its packages were installed, was not restarted and ignored Patrimeter's pool.
  • Two signatures deprecated by Symfony 7.4, which would have broken with Symfony 8: OwnedResourceVoter::voteOnAttribute() (Vote argument) and UserChecker::checkPostAuth() (token).

Batches 1 to 9 of v2 (original plan in the git history: docs/plan.md, removed after 2.3.0): technical foundation, complete CI, light/dark theme, multiple users with a second factor, data encryption, passkeys and FIDO2 keys, OAuth2/OIDC, properties and ownership shares.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
• PHP 8.3 minimum; PHPUnit 12, Doctrine DBAL 4.3 or later.
  • Installation reordered: scheduled tasks (§ 9), backup (§ 10), verification (§ 11), then update (§ 12: from git, from the CI archive, rollback, changing the PHP version).
  • New systemd services: patrimeter-scheduler and the patrimeter-alert@ template (installation § 9), reinstalled and restarted at every update. New variable: ADMIN_EMAIL.
  • Start from a new database: v1 data is not carried over. The migrations refuse a database containing unencrypted accounts.
  • Additional mandatory variables: AUTH_SECRET_KEY (openssl rand -base64 32) and DEFAULT_URI.
  • HTTPS mandatory, on the server or on a reverse proxy. Behind a proxy, TRUSTED_PROXIES is essential, and the proxy must pass Host, X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For.
  • New packages: php*-curl (OAuth) and sqlite3 (backups). Composer comes from its official phar (ci/install-composer.sh), no longer from the Debian package.
  • nginx: docs/nginx/patrimeter.conf is replaced by patrimeter-proxied.conf or patrimeter-tls.conf, plus the shared part patrimeter-app.conf to copy to /etc/nginx/snippets/.
  • bin/console app:set-password is replaced by app:user:create and app:user:set-password.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Sign-in with email address and password, then TOTP code (instead of the single password).
  • New passwords: at least 12 characters (10 before) and hard enough to guess.
  • Limiting attempts: counters per IP address, per account (delay without blocking) and global (blocking at 100 failures instead of 20, the global threshold now being shared by all users).
  • make serve serves AssetMapper's assets (tools/dev-server-router.php router).
  • Application ported to Symfony 7.4 LTS (Doctrine DBAL and Migrations, Twig, AssetMapper), without visible change: same addresses, same screens, same messages and same calculations, checked against a set of reference results frozen with v1.
  • PHP 8.3 to 8.5, installed from Ondřej Surý's repository; PHP 8.4 recommended.
  • Installation and update: Composer, .env.local file and Symfony console. bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate replaces bin/migrate.php, bin/console app:set-password replaces bin/set-password.php, and config.php is replaced by environment variables. The migrations are no longer applied automatically at the first request: they are part of the update procedure.
  • The php-fpm socket is now called /run/php/patrimeter.sock.
  • Chart.js 3.9.1 → 4.6.1 (3.x is no longer maintained).

items.title: Added
items.text:
• MCP: clients described by a metadata document (Client ID Metadata Documents), read by Symfony's HttpClient behind NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient, checked by the serializer and the validator.
  • Validation by Symfony Validator: account and property forms (Collection constraint), API request bodies read by #[MapRequestPayload] into classes with constraints (src/Application/Payload/). A decimal sent instead of an integer is now refused (it was truncated). The API requires Content-Type: application/json.
  • Scheduled tasks (symfony/scheduler, patrimeter-scheduler service): hourly purge of what has expired (links sent by email, log older than 180 days, API tokens, security cache) and PRAGMA optimize, instead of purges done during users' requests.
  • Email alerts to ADMIN_EMAIL: critical application error (Monolog, once per hour for the same error) and failure of a service, including the backup (OnFailure=, patrimeter-alert@ template).
  • New dependencies (Symfony): symfony/scheduler, symfony/messenger.
  • Leaked passwords refused (Symfony's NotCompromisedPassword, Have I Been Pwned API using k-anonymity); strength estimated by Symfony's PasswordStrength, at the same threshold as before.
  • Limiting attempts on symfony/rate-limiter (config/packages/rate_limiter.yaml): blocking after 5 failures per IP or 5 wrong codes over 15 minutes, 100 failures per hour in total, and per account one try per minute after 5 failures. The exponential delay from the first failure disappears. Counters and TOTP codes already used are in a cache pool on the database (cache_items table), kept by cache:clear: a code can no longer be used again just after an update.
  • New dependencies (Symfony): symfony/validator, symfony/rate-limiter, symfony/http-client.
  • CI: fast pipeline (about 15 min) on branches and merge requests; full pipeline on main, on a tag, on a schedule or with FULL_PIPELINE=1. Delivery archive built by the CI (release job, docs/installation.en.md § 12.2).
  • REST API and MCP service (docs/api.en.md), with the same authentication as the site: signing in in the browser and consenting (OAuth 2.1 authorization server, PKCE), or a personal token from the Security page. Bearer tokens through Symfony's native access_token authenticator; data decrypted with the key carried by the token, without the server being able to do it alone.
  • New dependencies: symfony/mcp-bundle and symfony/psr-http-message-bridge (Symfony), mcp/sdk (official MCP SDK), opis/json-schema, opis/string, opis/uri, php-http/discovery, psr/http-server-handler, psr/http-server-middleware. The bundle and the SDK are experimental.
  • Daily backup and restore (docs/backup.en.md): scripts and systemd timer, consistent live copy, integrity check, rotation by number of archives, protected restore.
  • deployment CI job: runs the installation and backup documentation on a fresh Debian 12, and checks nginx, php-fpm, HTTPS, permissions, restore and update from the outside.
  • Complete CI: Playwright journeys, authenticated ZAP, k6 load, Semgrep, Trivy, npm audit, GitLab SAST and Secret Detection templates, security gate with justified and dated exclusions, summary report, detection of N+1 queries, PHP 8.6 ahead of time (docs/ci.md).
  • The pipeline stops at the first job if the runner's disk is almost full.
  • Properties (Properties page, from Accounts): value of the property, share, value counted, outstanding principal and net value; a single form creating the property and its loans in one transaction; an existing loan is linked to a property from its page.
  • Ownership shares: history by effective month (100% by default), in millionths, rounded to the nearest cent. The total value of the property is still entered; the pyramid, the total and the history count the share in force each month. A linked loan counts prorata or as its own amount.
  • Multiple users, strictly separated: repositories filtered by owner, voter, composite foreign key (account_id, user_id), SQL forbidden outside the repositories (PHPStan rule), test robots going through every route with another user's identifiers.
  • Registration from the sign-in page (can be disabled, allowed domains configurable): confirmation link by email (24 h, single use) which also requires the chosen password. No answer reveals whether an address already has an account.
  • Mandatory TOTP second factor (QR code as SVG, key shown) and 10 single-use backup codes; TOTP secrets encrypted and codes protected by the AUTH_SECRET_KEY server key.
  • Security page: changing the password, changing the authenticator app, new backup codes, signing out the other sessions (after confirming the password within 5 minutes), sign-in log (180 days); alert emails.
  • Sessions limited to 12 hours after signing in, on top of the 30 minutes of inactivity.
  • Sending email through a configurable SMTP server (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, SMTP_ENCRYPTION, MAIL_FROM).
  • Encrypted data (names, types, dates, amounts) with a key per user, unreadable from the database, the backups or the sessions; recovery key shown once and confirmed; unlock screen. Details: docs/encryption.en.md.
  • Passkeys and FIDO2 security keys (web-auth/webauthn-lib 5.3): passwordless sign-in with user verification, or a key as second factor instead of the code. With the PRF extension, the passkey also unlocks the data; without it, the password is asked. Adding, renaming and deleting from the Security page. HTTPS mandatory in production.
  • OAuth2/OIDC sign-in (league/oauth2-client): Google, GitHub and a generic OIDC provider, active only if they are configured; PKCE, state, nonce. Never an automatic link based on the email address: it is done from the Security page. Account without a password: unlock passphrase mandatory. TOTP is still asked after OAuth. The last sign-in method cannot be removed.
  • Forgotten password: 30-minute link; data kept with the recovery key, erased after explicit confirmation otherwise.
  • Commands app:user:create, app:user:set-password, app:user:reset-2fa, app:user:rotate-key.
  • Sending emails after the response: the response time does not reveal whether an account exists.
  • Dependencies: scheb/2fa-bundle, scheb/2fa-totp and scheb/2fa-backup-code 7.14 (with spomky-labs/otphp), endroid/qr-code 6 (with bacon/bacon-qr-code), symfony/mailer and symfony/uid 7.4; all compatible with PHP 8.3 to 8.5 and under the MIT or BSD license.
  • Documentation: authentication flows (docs/auth-flows.md, in French) and data model (docs/data-model.md, in French).
  • Light or dark theme: button in the header of every page (sign-in included), system theme by default, choice remembered for a year in a cookie. The server writes the theme into the page: no flash on loading, no inline script. Without JavaScript, the button remains a form; with it, switching is instant and the chart is redrawn.
  • More than 370 PHPUnit tests: unit, integration, functional (real HTTP requests), non-regression against v1, architecture, migrations.
  • Quality tooling: PHP-CS-Fixer (PER Coding Style 3.0), PHPStan at the max level, Psalm with taint analysis, W3C validation of the rendered HTML and of the CSS.
  • GitLab continuous integration: lint, static analysis, tests on PHP 8.3 and 8.5, coverage with thresholds, W3C, composer audit, Gitleaks.
  • HSTS header over HTTPS, application log var/log/prod.log (14 days).
  • Documentation: architecture, continuous integration, security, v2 plan, environment variables (.env.example), Debian 12 procedure rewritten.

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• Restore: refused while the scheduled tasks run (they kept the database open and would have kept writing to the old one); the procedure stops patrimeter-scheduler together with php-fpm.
  • Scheduled tasks alert: restarted every 10 s without a reachable limit, the service never failed and its alert was never sent; it stops and sends a warning after 5 starts in 10 minutes.
  • Update (docs/installation.en.md § 12): service stopped during the operation and production cache deleted before any command (Symfony does not rebuild it by itself, and the one from the old version might no longer suit the new code); systemd units and backup scripts reinstalled. From the CI archive, /srv/patrimeter-v1 is no longer taken for the extracted archive.
  • Passkey without user verification accepted by reusing the second factor's challenge.
  • app:user:rotate-key: passkeys then opened the old key (error 500); also works with an unlock passphrase.
  • Forgotten password: a TOTP code already used was accepted.
  • Monthly entry: an account missing from the form (created since it was displayed) lost its balance for the month.
  • Amounts: 0.500 was read as €500.00; it is now refused.
  • A property with a share or loans can no longer change level, nor a linked loan become an asset, without removing them first: they kept applying without remaining editable.
  • Linking an external account from Security: refused by the CSP in Chrome and Edge, and session lost on return.
  • Properties: same opening and closing rule as the dashboard.
  • Registration: beyond the quota, the links already received remain valid, and the first email counts among the three per hour.
  • Errors 500: /?mois=1900-03, address a..b@example.com (which also left an orphan row), invalid property or passkey name.
  • CI: merge request pipeline refused by GitLab (jobs of the SAST and Secret Detection templates missing), hence no pipeline on a branch whose merge request is open.

  • Installation: http2 on refused by Debian 12's nginx 1.22, OAuth sign-in in error 500 without php-curl, log name, private repository, reverse proxy missing from the procedure.

  • A FIDO2 key without a resident identifier was refused as second factor: it returns no userHandle, whereas the user is already identified. Found by the Playwright journeys.

  • The Accounts page looked empty for a signed-in user: a navigation variable overwrote the list (templates/base.html.twig).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• A user's data inaccessible to the others (separation in five barriers, see docs/architecture.md, in French); links sent by email built from DEFAULT_URI, never from the request's Host header.
  • Migrations written in SQL only: Doctrine's automatic schema comparison is disabled, because under SQLite it rebuilt tables and triggered cascades.
First version: native PHP, SQLite, single user.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Accounts and loans with a predefined type, pyramid level, nature, opening and archiving.
  • Monthly entry of all accounts in one form, with the last balance carried over automatically.
  • Dashboard: SVG pyramid, net worth, change over one month and over one year, month selector as a calendar.
  • History: net worth curve or areas by level, over several periods.
  • Authentication with a single password (Argon2id), limited attempts, hardened sessions, CSRF token, security headers including a strict CSP.

items.title: Reporting a vulnerability
items.text:
Report any vulnerability through a private vulnerability report on GitHub: https://github.com/kartnico/patrimeter/security/advisories/new.

  • Response within 7 days: acknowledgement, then assessment of the severity.
  • Fix published in a new version as soon as possible, within 90 days at the latest for a confirmed vulnerability; the CHANGELOG and the Release mention it.
  • Coordinated disclosure: please do not publish any detail before the fix; the person who reported the vulnerability is credited if they wish.

Only the latest published version receives security fixes.

items.title: Current state
items.text: Patrimeter is multi-user: separated accounts, mandatory password and TOTP second factor, wealth data encrypted with a key per user (docs/encryption.en.md), passkeys and FIDO2 keys. Authentication flows: docs/auth-flows.md (in French). Backups: docs/backup.en.md.

items.title: What is protected
items.text:
• Each user's wealth data: accounts, amounts, history, invisible and inaccessible to the other users.
  • Access to the accounts: password, second factor, sessions.
  • The confidentiality of registrations: the application does not reveal whether an address has an account.

items.title: Assumptions
items.text:
• The server administrator is trusted (see the limits below).
  • HTTPS is mandatory in production, on the server or on a reverse proxy declared in TRUSTED_PROXIES: passkeys and the __Host- cookie do not exist without it.
  • Dependencies come from recognised sources (Surý repository, Packagist, versioned composer.lock).

items.title: Sign-in log
items.text: Each user sees, on their My account page, their last 30 events (kept for 180 days): sign-ins, wrong passwords and codes, backup codes used, identity confirmations, changes of password, app or codes, closing the other sessions. Only the type, the success, the IP address, the browser and the date are recorded, never a secret.

items.title: Known limits
items.text:
• Active administrator: encryption protects against passive access (database, backups, sessions, logs). An administrator who changes the code can capture a password at the next sign-in; no web application escapes this.
  • Metadata visible to the administrator: email addresses, number of accounts, statements and ownership shares, months entered, number of budget categories and items and the months in which its amounts were saved, number of members of a family account, number of savings goals, order of the budget's categories and items, day of the monthly reminder chosen, whether a Carbure link exists, technical dates, sign-in log, open sessions (IP address, browser, dates) and trusted browsers. The app:user:list command shows part of it (addresses, dates, number of accounts, last sign-in), without decrypting anything.
  • Carbure: the instance address comes from the user. Patrimeter only calls …/api/mcp, with POST, without redirects, with a bounded delay and size, never sends back the response, and limits calls per user; CARBURE_ALLOWED_HOSTS restricts the hosts on an instance open to the public.
  • Password lost without a recovery key: the data is permanently lost.
  • Demo mode: off by default; turned on (DEMO_MODE=true), it lets anyone who reaches the sign-in page create a temporary account. Only turn it on for an instance dedicated to the demo (settings).
  • Leaked passwords: the check queries the Have I Been Pwned API (only the first 5 characters of the SHA-1 hash). Server without outbound access or service unreachable: it is skipped, and only the entropy is checked.
  • Without HTTPS, the password, the code and the session cookie travel in clear on the network. Behind a reverse proxy, the last hop to the server remains HTTP: keep it to a trusted network, and restrict it to the proxy's address (allow in the virtual host).
  • API token: whoever holds it reads the data in clear until it expires or is revoked. An MCP client sends what it reads to its provider.
  • Experimental libraries: symfony/mcp-bundle and mcp/sdk do not guarantee compatibility between versions yet; the MCP service is checked in the CI at every update.
  • Email alerts: the message of a critical error goes to ADMIN_EMAIL. It contains no secret or wealth data (filtered logs, encrypted data), but may mention an IP address or a path.
  • Restoring a backup: passwords, TOTP and recovery keys go back to their state at the time, and what was deleted since reappears (docs/backup.en.md).
  • Limiting by IP address: behind a reverse proxy, TRUSTED_PROXIES and X-Forwarded-For are essential, otherwise all attempts seem to come from the proxy and share the same counter.
  • Global block: 100 failures in one hour, all addresses together, block all sign-ins until the oldest ones leave this sliding hour; this is deliberate (distributed attack), at the cost of a possible denial of service.

items.title: Installing Patrimeter (administrator)
items.text:
Two ways, at your choice:

  • With Docker: download compose.yaml and patrimeter.env.example from docker/, configure patrimeter.env from the template, then run docker compose up -d (Installing with Docker).
  • On Linux: the archive of a version, with PHP and nginx (Installing on Linux).

Either way, you need HTTPS access (reverse proxy or certificate) and, ideally, an SMTP server for the emails. On the first visit, the installation wizard checks the configuration and creates the first account, yours.

Updating: one command, the database being backed up automatically first (updating).

items.title: Starting to track your net worth (user)
items.text:
1. Create your account from the sign-in page ("Create an account"), then confirm your address with the link received by email. → First sign-in
  2. Set up your authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password…) by scanning the QR code, and write down your backup codes.
  3. Write down your recovery key: it is what saves your data if you forget your password.
  4. Create your accounts and loans: current account, savings accounts, life insurance, PEA, consumer loan… Your properties and their loans are created in the Real estate tab of My account. → Accounts
  5. Enter their balances for the month. → Monthly update
  6. Look at your pyramid on the Net worth page, then come back every month: the Monthly update menu reminds you as long as the month is not entered. → Net worth and history
  7. Set yourself goals (Monthly update, Goals tab) and follow them in the Goals menu; and, if you wish, the household budget. → Savings goals, budget

To discover Patrimeter without an account: Try the demo on the sign-in page, if the instance offers it (trying without an account).

items.title: API reference
items.text:
Patrimeter's REST API: JSON, amounts in cents (integers), months in YYYY-MM format, dates in YYYY-MM-DD format. The data is that of the token's user, and theirs alone: another user's account answers 404, like an account that does not exist.

Authentication: bearer token (Authorization: Bearer patrimeter_…), personal token created on the "My account" page or OAuth 2.1 token (authorization code with PKCE). Scopes: patrimeter.read (reading) and patrimeter.write (writing, includes reading). Rate: 120 requests in a row per token, then one per second.

Request bodies are JSON (Content-Type: application/json, otherwise 415). A decimal number where an integer is expected is rejected, never truncated. Errors in application/problem+json format (RFC 9457). Error titles, account type labels and level names are in French.

Base address: https://patrimeter.example.org/api/v1 (replace the origin with that of your installation). User guide, OAuth and MCP service: REST API and MCP service.

Complete OpenAPI 3.1.0 description, to import into a client (Bruno, Insomnia, Postman…) or a code generator: openapi.yaml.

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
• personalToken: Personal token (patrimeter_…), created on the "My account" page, "API and applications" section, read only or read and write, for 30, 90 or 365 days.
  • oauth: OAuth 2.1: authorization code with PKCE (S256), public client, audience <DEFAULT_URI>/api (RFC 8707). Discovery: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api, then /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server. Scopes: patrimeter.read (Read the net worth, accounts, statements and shares); patrimeter.write (Create, update and delete (includes reading)).
