items.title: REST API and MCP service
items.text:
Two ways to access the same data, with the same authentication mechanisms as the site, the user signing in in their browser (password and TOTP, or passkey):

  • REST API: /api/v1/…, JSON, amounts in cents (integers), months in YYYY-MM format.
  • MCP service: /mcp, for an assistant or an MCP client. Revision 2026-07-28, and earlier revisions for older clients, through symfony/mcp-bundle (experimental: pinned in composer.lock).

items.title: Enabling
items.text:
The API and the MCP service are disabled by default, each by its environment variable, as in Carbure: an instance only exposes its pages until the administrator decides otherwise. In .env.local (installation § 3) or the container's environment file:

API_ENABLED=true   # REST API, /api/v1/…
MCP_ENABLED=true   # MCP service, /mcp

A disabled service answers 404 on all its addresses, before routing and the firewall (Http\ApiAvailabilitySubscriber), OAuth metadata included. The OAuth authorization server (/oauth/…, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) and personal tokens (My account page) only exist if one of the two is enabled. Tokens already issued stay in the database and work again if the service is enabled again.

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Patrimeter is its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server: authorization code with PKCE (S256), public clients, bearer token. The firewall uses Symfony's native access_token authenticator.

Access How to get it Lifetime Application, MCP client OAuth flow: the browser opens on the site's sign-in, then the consent Access token 1 h, refresh token 30 days (single use) Script Personal token created from the My account page, after confirming your identity 30, 90 or 365 days

In both cases: Authorization: Bearer patrimeter_….

  • Recognizable format: a token always starts with patrimeter_, followed by 24 hexadecimal characters, _ and 43 base64url characters. A secret detector thus spots a token published by mistake (code repository, ticket, log): the patrimeter-api-token rule of .gitleaks.toml applies it to this repository, and its regular expression can be reused in any other tool. Tokens of the former format (pm1.…, before 2.23.0) stay valid until they expire. An exposed token is revoked from the "AI agents" tab.

  • Scopes: patrimeter.read (default), patrimeter.write (writing, includes reading). Without the right scope: 403 and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope".

  • Audience (RFC 8707): an OAuth token is only valid for its resource, <DEFAULT_URI>/mcp or <DEFAULT_URI>/api. A personal token is valid for both.
  • End of validity: like a session, a token stops working if the password changes, if the user signs out their other sessions, or if the administrator resets their second factor.
  • Revoking: My account page, "AI agents" tab, or POST /oauth/revoke.
  • Encryption: the token opens the user's data key for the request, without the server being able to do it alone: the database only holds its hash and a copy of the key wrapped under a key derived from it (encryption.md). Whoever holds a token reads the data in clear: treat it like a password.

Discovery, for a client: a request without a token answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…", which leads to /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp (or /api), then to /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server. Two ways for a client to make itself known:

  • Metadata document (Client ID Metadata Document, preferred by the MCP specification): its client_id is the HTTPS address of a JSON document (client_id, redirect_uris, client_name). The server reads it with Symfony's HttpClient, never towards the local network or the loopback, without redirects, 64 KB at most, and keeps it for an hour. The server must be able to reach the address of the document.
  • Dynamic registration (RFC 7591) on POST /oauth/register, limited to 10 per hour and per IP address.

Redirect addresses over HTTPS, or over HTTP on the loopback.

The reverse proxy must pass /mcp, /api/, /oauth/ and /.well-known/oauth-, and the Authorization header. As the site remains restricted to the local network, a client must be there too.

items.title: REST API
items.text:
Complete description in OpenAPI 3.1 format: openapi.yaml, to import into a client (Bruno, Insomnia, Postman…) or a code generator. Its readable version, with each operation, its parameters, its responses and its schemas: API reference (online documentation). A test checks that the description covers exactly the API routes and that the actual responses follow its schemas.

With curl, a personal token in $TOKEN:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://patrimeter.example.org/api/v1/net-worth
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X PUT \
    -d '{"amount_cents": 1234567}' https://patrimeter.example.org/api/v1/accounts/12/statements/2026-11
Method and address Role GET /api/v1/me User of the token, write permission GET /api/v1/account-types Account types, default level and nature GET /api/v1/net-worth?month= Net worth, by level (current month by default) GET /api/v1/history?from=&to= Net worth month by month GET /api/v1/properties?month= Properties: value, share, loans, net value GET /api/v1/goals?month= Savings goals: value reached, effort needed, pace, status, projected month GET /api/v1/challenges Challenges and stars of the month: stars and level, saver stage and style, entry streak, each challenge with its thresholds; with the "not investment advice" notice GET /api/v1/budget?month= Household budget in force: totals, categories and items with their amount GET, POST /api/v1/accounts List, creation (name, type_id, opened_on, and optional level, nature, initial_amount_cents) GET, PUT, DELETE /api/v1/accounts/{id} Details with statements and shares, update, deletion POST /api/v1/accounts/{id}/archive, /unarchive Closing (closed_on), reactivation PUT /api/v1/accounts/{id}/loan-link Links a loan to a property (asset_id, loan_mode: prorata or own), or unlinks it (null asset_id) GET /api/v1/accounts/{id}/statements Statements PUT, DELETE /api/v1/accounts/{id}/statements/{month} Statement of a month (amount_cents). A loan has a positive amount: the outstanding principal GET /api/v1/accounts/{id}/shares Shares of a property PUT, DELETE /api/v1/accounts/{id}/shares/{month} Share from a month on (share_millionths, from 1 to 1,000,000)

Request bodies are JSON (Content-Type: application/json, otherwise 415), read and validated by #[MapRequestPayload] and Symfony's constraints. A decimal number where an integer is expected is rejected, never truncated.

Errors in application/problem+json format (RFC 9457): {"title", "status"}, and errors (field → message) for rejected data (422). Another user's account answers 404, like an account that does not exist.

items.title: MCP service
items.text:
Address to give the client: https://patrimeter.example.org/mcp. It opens the browser for signing in and consenting. For example with Claude Code:

claude mcp add --transport http patrimeter https://patrimeter.example.org/mcp
Tool Scope Role get_net_worth read Net worth of a month, by level get_history read Net worth month by month list_accounts, get_account read Accounts, values; statements and shares of an account list_properties read Properties and net value list_goals read Savings goals and where each one stands get_challenges read Challenges and stars of the month, with the "not investment advice" notice get_budget read Household budget of the month list_account_types read Account types create_account, save_statement, delete_statement write Creating an account, statement of a month

A write tool called with a read token answers 403: the client then asks for access again with the write scope. An assistant that calls these tools sends your data to its provider: the consent covers this too.

Origin: as the MCP specification asks against DNS rebinding, a request carrying an Origin header (sent by a browser) is only accepted if it is the site's address (DEFAULT_URI) or one of the origins of MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS; otherwise: 403, before the token is even read. A client outside a browser (Claude Code, script) sends no such header and is not concerned.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
• Rate per token: 120 requests in a row, then one per second (API and MCP together). Beyond that, 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After (seconds) and {"title": "Trop de requêtes", "status": 429, "retry_after": …} (error titles are in French).
  • The sign-in log records access granted or revoked, not each call.

items.title: Backup and restore
items.text: All commands are run as root. The CI runs this page on a real deployment: backup, data change, restore, then signing in and reading the restored data (deployment job, see ci.md, in French). The commands are the same as in the French version of this page.

items.title: What to back up
items.text:
Item How Why Database /srv/patrimeter/var/patrimeter.sqlite Every day, § 1 All the data: accounts, statements, users, key envelopes /srv/patrimeter/.env.local Once, by hand, in a password manager AUTH_SECRET_KEY is only there: without it, TOTP must be set up again (§ 7) TLS certificate, if the server holds one (installation, § 6.2) By hand Saves requesting it again

Everything else is regenerated and is not backed up: code, vendor/, public/assets/, var/cache/, var/sessions/, var/log/. The files installed in /etc/systemd/system/ and /usr/local/sbin/ come from the archive (docs/) and are reinstalled at every update.

Never copy the database with cp while the application is running: in WAL mode, part of the recent data is in the -wal file, and the copy may be inconsistent. The script uses SQLite's backup API, which works on a live database.

Content of an archive: wealth data is encrypted in it, and unreadable without each user's password (encryption.md). What remains in clear text: email addresses, password hashes, the sign-in log (IP addresses) and the months entered. Do not put the archives somewhere you do not control without encrypting them. Keep .env.local elsewhere: stealing an archive then does not give away the TOTP secrets either.

items.title: 1. Setting up
items.text:
The sqlite3 command is one of the requirements.

install -m 0755 /srv/patrimeter/docs/backup/patrimeter-backup.sh /usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-backup
install -m 0755 /srv/patrimeter/docs/backup/patrimeter-restore.sh /usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-restore
install -m 0644 /srv/patrimeter/docs/backup/patrimeter-backup.service /etc/systemd/system/patrimeter-backup.service
install -m 0644 /srv/patrimeter/docs/backup/patrimeter-backup.timer /etc/systemd/system/patrimeter-backup.timer
install -m 0644 /srv/patrimeter/docs/backup/patrimeter-restore-check.service /etc/systemd/system/patrimeter-restore-check.service
install -m 0644 /srv/patrimeter/docs/backup/patrimeter-restore-check.timer /etc/systemd/system/patrimeter-restore-check.timer
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now patrimeter-backup.timer patrimeter-restore-check.timer
systemctl start patrimeter-backup.service   # first backup, right away

Checking:

systemctl list-timers patrimeter-backup.timer       # next run
journalctl -u patrimeter-backup.service -n 5 --no-pager
ls -lh /var/backups/patrimeter/

Every night at 03:15, the script copies the database, checks the copy (PRAGMA integrity_check), compresses it into /var/backups/patrimeter/patrimeter-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.sqlite.gz (UTC time) with its .sha256 hash, and keeps the last 30 archives. Rotation is by count, not by age: if backups stop, the last ones remain. If the server is off at 03:15, the backup runs when it starts again.

To keep another number of archives, systemctl edit patrimeter-backup.service, then:

[Service]
Environment=PATRIMETER_BACKUP_KEEP=60

items.title: 2. Copying off the server
items.text:
Archives on the same server as the database protect neither from losing it nor from a dead disk. Set up one of these copies.

Copy encrypted by Patrimeter (recommended): after each backup, the archive is encrypted with age for one or more public keys, then handed to a copy command of your choice (rsync, scp, rclone…). The server never has the private key: an archive copied elsewhere can only be read with it. Without encryption, the copy command is refused.

  1. On the machine that will keep the copies (or a safe computer): apt-get install age, then age-keygen -o patrimeter-sauvegarde.key. The command shows the public key (age1…). Keep the private key off the server (password manager, vault): without it, the copies are unreadable.
  2. On the server, apt-get install age, then systemctl edit patrimeter-backup.service:
[Service]
Environment=PATRIMETER_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENTS=age1…
Environment='PATRIMETER_BACKUP_COPY=rsync -a "$1" sauvegarde@nas.lan:patrimeter/'
  • PATRIMETER_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENTS: one or more public keys separated by spaces, or the absolute path of a file holding one per line.
  • PATRIMETER_BACKUP_COPY: command run as root, which receives the encrypted archive as $1, or as its last argument if it does not mention $1 (/var/backups/patrimeter/chiffrees/patrimeter-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.sqlite.gz.age). Without it, the encrypted archives stay in that folder, ready to be pulled from another machine.
  • Run a backup (systemctl start patrimeter-backup.service) and check the copy. To read it back, on the machine of the private key: age --decrypt -i patrimeter-sauvegarde.key archive.sqlite.gz.age > archive.sqlite.gz.

A failing copy makes the backup fail: email alert, and the monitoring reports a backup that is too old (supervision.md). The local archive, for its part, is made.

Other options:

  • Backup of the whole server (virtual machine snapshot, system backup…): schedule it after 03:15. /var/backups/patrimeter/ is part of it. After restoring the server, start again from an archive (§ 4) rather than from the database, which may have been copied in the middle of a write.
  • Copy pulled from another machine: that machine does the reading, so a compromised server cannot erase its copies. rsync package and SSH key on its side, rsync on the server. With the encryption above and no copy command, pull only chiffrees/:
# On the backup machine, every day after 03:15.
rsync -a --ignore-existing --exclude 'avant-restauration-*' \
    root@<server address>:/var/backups/patrimeter/ /path/to/backups/patrimeter/

items.title: 3. Monitoring and checking
items.text:
A failed backup sends an email to ADMIN_EMAIL (OnFailure=, see installation, § 7), if SMTP is configured. A backup that no longer starts at all warns nobody: watch for it too, with your monitoring or by hand:

systemctl is-failed patrimeter-backup.service      # "failed" if the last one failed
find /var/backups/patrimeter -name 'patrimeter-*.sqlite.gz' -mtime -2 | grep -q . && echo 'recent' || echo 'TOO OLD'

Full check of an archive, without changing anything: hash, decompression, integrity, foreign keys, compatibility with the installed code.

ARCHIVE="$(find /var/backups/patrimeter -maxdepth 1 -name 'patrimeter-*.sqlite.gz' | sort | tail -n 1)"
/usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-restore --check "$ARCHIVE"

This same check runs on its own on the 1st of every month (patrimeter-restore-check.timer, at 04:30, on the latest archive): a failure sends an email to ADMIN_EMAIL. To run it right away: systemctl start patrimeter-restore-check.service.

This check covers the structure: the administrator cannot decrypt the data. Only a user signing in proves it: run a test restore on a throwaway server (§ 5) from time to time.

items.title: 4. Restoring on the same server
items.text:
The service is stopped during the restore (nginx answers 502), scheduled tasks included: they keep the database open. Replace $ARCHIVE with the archive you want if it is not the latest one, found in § 3. Set PHP to the installed version.

PHP=8.5
systemctl stop "php$PHP-fpm" patrimeter-scheduler.service
/usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-restore "$ARCHIVE"
systemctl start "php$PHP-fpm" patrimeter-scheduler.service

The script refuses an invalid archive or one more recent than the code, and refuses to run while php-fpm or the scheduled tasks are active. It keeps the replaced database in /var/backups/patrimeter/avant-restauration-…/ ("before restore"), deletes the -wal and -shm files, closes the sessions and applies the missing migrations. If php-fpm crashed, an orphan socket may remain: delete /run/php/patrimeter.sock once php-fpm has really stopped.

To undo, with php-fpm and the scheduled tasks stopped:

cp -p /var/backups/patrimeter/avant-restauration-…/patrimeter.sqlite* /srv/patrimeter/var/

These folders are not rotated: delete them once all is well.

After a failed update, the code must first go back to the previous version: mise-a-jour.en.md.

items.title: 5. Restoring on a new server
items.text:
1. Follow the installation up to § 3 included, with a version at least as recent as the archive, and your .env.local put back into /srv/patrimeter/.
  2. Do § 5 and 6, but not § 7 yet: the scheduled tasks would open the database.
  3. Put the archive on the server and restore:
# Installed PHP version, and archive to restore (example)
PHP=8.5
ARCHIVE=/tmp/patrimeter-20270115-031500.sqlite.gz
# Restore command, then the restore, php-fpm stopped
install -m 0755 /srv/patrimeter/docs/backup/patrimeter-restore.sh /usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-restore
systemctl stop "php$PHP-fpm"
/usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-restore "$ARCHIVE"
systemctl start "php$PHP-fpm"
  1. Finish with § 7 of the installation, the backup (§ 1 and 2 of this page) and the check. Finally, point the reverse proxy to the new address: on the same domain, the passkeys keep working.

items.title: 6. What a restore changes for users
items.text:
The whole database goes back to the date of the archive, for all users. To tell them:

  • entries and accounts created since are lost; user accounts created since no longer exist;
  • sign-in methods also go back to that date: a password changed since becomes the old one again, and the same goes for the TOTP app, the backup codes and the recovery key. A passkey added since is no longer recognised: remove it from the device, then register it again;
  • what was deleted since reappears, including data erased by a "forgotten password";
  • API access revoked since becomes valid again if it has not expired: after a restore following a stolen token, have the access revoked and created again from the My account page. Access granted since no longer exists;
  • everyone is signed out;
  • sign-in attempt counters also go back to that date (they are in the database).

items.title: 7. If .env.local is lost
items.text:
Create it again as in § 3 of the installation. The data remains readable: it depends on each user's password, not on this file.

  • A new APP_SECRET has no effect on the data.
  • With a new AUTH_SECRET_KEY, every password sign-in ends on an error page for the accounts that have TOTP, because its secret can no longer be read. Reset each account, after checking the identity of its holder if you are not alone on this server; they will set up a new app at their next sign-in:
runuser -u www-data -- sqlite3 /srv/patrimeter/var/patrimeter.sqlite 'SELECT email FROM users;'
runuser -u www-data -- php /srv/patrimeter/bin/console app:user:reset-2fa <email>

items.title: Installing with Docker
items.text: Patrimeter runs in three containers described by compose.yaml: the application, the scheduled tasks and the daily backup. The commands run as root (or as a user of the docker group).

items.title: 1. Requirements
items.text:
• Linux with Docker and Docker Compose (or Podman 4.7 or newer, with podman compose).
  • The public Docker Hub repository name from the release README; no GitLab account is needed.
  • An HTTPS reverse proxy in front of the container: HTTPS is mandatory.
  • Optional: an SMTP server, for the emails (registrations, forgotten password, alerts).

items.title: 2. Installing
items.text:
Open the version tag in the public GitHub repository. Download compose.yaml and patrimeter.env.example from the docker/ directory. Replace kartnico1/patrimeter below with the published repository.

# Folder of the installation, with the two downloaded files
mkdir -p /srv/patrimeter-docker
cd /srv/patrimeter-docker
# Configuration from the template, readable by root only
printf 'PATRIMETER_IMAGE=docker.io/kartnico1/patrimeter:latest\n' > .env
cp patrimeter.env.example patrimeter.env
chmod 600 patrimeter.env
# Two secrets to copy into patrimeter.env: APP_SECRET, then AUTH_SECRET_KEY
openssl rand -hex 32
openssl rand -base64 32

In patrimeter.env, also set:

  • DEFAULT_URI: the public address of the site, in https://;
  • TRUSTED_PROXIES: the address of the reverse proxy;
  • SMTP_*, MAIL_FROM and ADMIN_EMAIL, for the emails.

Keep a copy of patrimeter.env off the server: without AUTH_SECRET_KEY, the users must set up their authenticator app again.

items.title: 3. Starting
items.text:
cd /srv/patrimeter-docker
# Start the three services
docker compose up -d
# Status of the services: "app" must be "healthy"
docker compose ps

Only app has an HTTP probe. scheduler and backup should be running, without a healthy status. To check their activity, inspect docker compose logs scheduler backup.

The container serves the site over HTTP on port 8080. The reverse proxy publishes it over HTTPS, for example with nginx:

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name patrimeter.example.fr;
    # ssl_certificate and ssl_certificate_key: your certificate

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port 443;
    }
}

Finally open the site: the installation wizard checks the configuration (HTTPS, address of the site, sending emails, alerts) and creates the first account, yours. The next accounts: "Create an account" on the sign-in page, or docker compose exec app patrimeter-console app:user:create you@example.com. To change a setting later (demonstration mode, email server…): Settings.

items.title: 4. Updating
items.text:
First read the Installation part of the CHANGELOG for each newer version.

cd /srv/patrimeter-docker
# Image of the latest version
docker compose pull
# Restart: the "app" container backs up the database, then applies the migrations
docker compose up -d

On every new version, the database is backed up before any change, in the data volume (var/backups-before-update, the latest three). The bottom of every page shows the installed version.

Optional automatic rollout (Docker Compose v2): after testing your backups, schedule docker compose pull && docker compose up -d --wait from the installation directory. Monitor failures. This follows the selected tag and preserves named volumes; never use down -v. A digest stays pinned.

Rolling back: restart on the image of the previous version, then restore the backup made before the update.

cd /srv/patrimeter-docker
# Previous version (example)
export PATRIMETER_IMAGE=docker.io/kartnico1/patrimeter:vX.Y.Z
# Stop, then restore the latest backup made before the update
docker compose stop app scheduler backup
docker compose run --rm --no-deps app sh -c \
    'patrimeter-restore "$(ls var/backups-before-update/patrimeter-*.sqlite.gz | sort | tail -n 1)"'
# Restart on the previous version
docker compose up -d

items.title: 5. Backing up and restoring
items.text:
The backup service backs up the database into the backups volume (30 archives kept), then checks the latest archive. If both operations succeed, the next backup runs 24 hours later by default (PATRIMETER_BACKUP_INTERVAL, in seconds). If either the backup or the check fails, the service logs the failure and starts a new backup one hour later. Copy the archives and patrimeter.env off the server (backup).

cd /srv/patrimeter-docker
# Immediate backup, then list of the archives
docker compose exec backup patrimeter-backup
docker compose exec backup ls -l /var/backups/patrimeter

Restoring an archive:

cd /srv/patrimeter-docker
# Archive to restore (example)
ARCHIVE=/var/backups/patrimeter/patrimeter-20270115-031500.sqlite.gz
# Stop, check the archive, restore, restart
docker compose stop app scheduler backup
docker compose run --rm --no-deps backup patrimeter-restore --check "$ARCHIVE"
docker compose run --rm --no-deps backup patrimeter-restore "$ARCHIVE"
docker compose up -d

items.title: 6. Podman
items.text: compose.yaml works as is with podman compose, even without root: then keep port 8080 (a port above 1024).

items.title: What is guaranteed
items.text:
Passive access is not enough to read wealth data: the database, backups, session files and logs contain no account names, types, dates or amounts in clear text, nor anything of the household budget (first names, categories, items, income, amounts).

Limit: an active administrator who changes the code can capture a password at the next sign-in, or read PHP's memory. This is true of any web application, including with encryption in the browser, since the server would then provide the JavaScript.

What remains visible: email addresses, number of accounts, statements and ownership shares, months entered, number of budget categories and items and the months in which its amounts were saved, technical dates, sign-in log, open sessions (IP address, browser, dates).

items.title: Key hierarchy
items.text:
libsodium only, no home-made cryptography.

flowchart TD
    P[Password] -->|Argon2id, 64 MiB, 3 passes, own salt| E1[Password envelope]
    R[Recovery key, 256 bits] -->|HKDF-SHA256, own salt| E2[Recovery envelope]
    K2[Passkey with the PRF extension] -->|HKDF-SHA256, own salt| E3[Passkey envelope]
    E3 --> D
    E1 --> D[Data key: 256 bits, one per user]
    E2 --> D
    D -->|XChaCha20-Poly1305, random nonce| C[Accounts, statements, budget, savings goals, family account members, Carbure link]
    D -->|envelope in the session| S[Server session]
    K[Random session key, HttpOnly cookie] --> S
  • Data: each ciphertext is bound to its table, its row, its owner and a version (associated data): copied elsewhere or modified, it does not decrypt.
  • Family account: a member's imported export file is encrypted with the family account's data key (context family_members:<row>:<owner>:1); the member's account has no access to it, and the family account never reads the member's data anywhere but in this file.
  • Creation: the data key is created at the first sign-in, the only moment when the password is known. A registration that was never confirmed therefore has no key.
  • During the session: the key is wrapped again under a random key that only lives in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (Secure over HTTPS). The server only keeps the envelope and rebuilds the key at every request. Reading var/sessions is not enough to decrypt.
  • Demo accounts (DEMO_MODE): random data key, without any envelope; it only lives in the session, and the account is deleted at sign-out or when it expires.
  • API and MCP tokens: each token carries a copy of the data key, wrapped under a key derived from its secret (HKDF-SHA256), which the server does not keep; it only keeps its hash. See api.md.
  • TOTP secrets: readable before unlocking, so encrypted with the AUTH_SECRET_KEY server key. They are protected against a database leak, not against root.
  • Password change: only the envelope is redone, the data is not encrypted again.
  • Rotation (compromise): bin/console app:user:rotate-key <email> encrypts everything again with a new key and closes the sessions. Only the password provided wraps the new key: the recovery key is cancelled, and passkeys no longer unlock until they are registered again.

items.title: Consequences for users
items.text: Situation Consequence Forgotten password, recovery key available Data kept (email + key). With a valid code, TOTP is kept; without a code, it must be set up again. Forgotten password, no key Access restored (email + code), but data permanently erased after confirmation. The administrator cannot recover anything. Lost phone Backup codes; failing that, email + recovery key. Passkey without PRF (support varies between browsers) Sign-in possible, then the password is asked to unlock. Session cookie lost Unlock screen: the password is asked again.

items.title: For the administrator
items.text:
• app:user:set-password cannot keep the data without the old password: --erase-data is required as soon as the account has a key.
  • Losing AUTH_SECRET_KEY makes the TOTP secrets unreadable (app:user:reset-2fa for each user), but not the data.
  • No rollback of the migration once data has been encrypted.

items.title: Exporting and importing data
items.text: Users can export all their data into a file, then import it on another Patrimeter instance (moving, new server): Your data page, from My account.

items.title: Content of the file
items.text:
UTF-8 JSON, unencrypted: the server decrypts the data with the key of the signed-in user. Keep it somewhere safe and delete it after use. The export requires a recent confirmation of identity (password, 5 minutes).

{
  "format": "patrimeter",
  "version": 4,
  "exported_on": "2026-11-13",
  "accounts": [
    {
      "ref": 12,
      "name": "Maison",
      "type": "residence_principale",
      "level": "residence",
      "nature": "asset",
      "opened_on": "2020-03-01",
      "closed_on": null,
      "linked_asset_ref": null,
      "loan_mode": null,
      "statements": [{"month": "2026-10", "amount_cents": 32000000}],
      "shares": [{"month": "2020-03", "share_millionths": 500000}]
    }
  ],
  "budget": {
    "adults": ["Flo", "Nico"],
    "adult_birth_years": [1985, 1983],
    "children": [{"ref": 1, "name": "Eva", "birth_year": 2009}],
    "precaution_months": 4,
    "categories": [
      {
        "name": "Épargne du foyer",
        "group": "savings",
        "adult": null,
        "lines": [{"ref": 31, "name": "Épargne de précaution", "child_ref": null, "account_ref": 14}]
      }
    ],
    "months": [
      {
        "month": "2026-11",
        "incomes": [{"adult": 1, "amount_cents": 186000}, {"adult": 2, "amount_cents": 414300}],
        "split_rule": "fixed",
        "first_adult_share_millionths": 275000,
        "amounts": [{"line_ref": 31, "amount_cents": 30000}],
        "child_incomes": [{"child_ref": 1, "amount_cents": 45000}]
      }
    ]
  },
  "goals": [
    {
      "name": "Down payment",
      "target_cents": 2000000,
      "target_month": "2028-06",
      "scope": "accounts",
      "level": null,
      "account_refs": [14],
      "start_month": "2026-05",
      "start_cents": 600000
    }
  ],
  "indicators": [
    {
      "name": "Retraite",
      "levels": ["actions"],
      "account_refs": [14],
      "share_of_net_worth": true
    }
  ]
}
  • ref: identifier of the account in the file; linked_asset_ref refers to it for a loan linked to a property.
  • type: code of the account type (the same on every instance), not its number.
  • Amounts in cents, shares in millionths (500,000 = 50%), as in the API.
  • budget: the household budget (user guide, Household budget page), or null. Adults numbered in order (1, then 2 for a couple); group is needs, wants or savings (50/30/20 rule); a category's adult: null for the shared budget, otherwise the adult's number. An item's child_ref and account_ref refer to the children and accounts of the file, an amount's line_ref to an item. split_rule: income (in proportion to income) or fixed (fixed share of the first adult, first_adult_share_millionths). Since Patrimeter 2.26: adult_birth_years (in the order of the adults) and a child's birth_year, years of birth (null if unknown); a month's child_incomes, incomes of a child of working age (16 in the year), child_ref referring to the child. Absent from an older file, which is imported as it is.
  • goals: the savings goals; scope is net (net worth), level (level level) or accounts (accounts of the file, account_refs); the starting point (start_month, start_cents) is kept as it is.
  • indicators (since Patrimeter 3.4): the custom indicators, their levels (levels) and their accounts of the file (account_refs).
  • <, >, &, ' and " are written \u003C, \u003E…: entered text can never be taken for HTML; the file reads back identically.

Not exported: the user account itself (address, password, second factor, passkeys, API tokens), which is created again on the other instance.

items.title: Import
items.text:
• Into an account that is still empty: the import does not merge with existing accounts, nor with an existing budget.
  • A version 1 file (Patrimeter 2.7 and earlier, without a budget), 2 (Patrimeter 2.17 and earlier, without goals) or 3 (Patrimeter 3.3 and earlier, without indicators) can still be imported.
  • All or nothing: at the slightest rejection (unknown type, month outside the opening period…), nothing is imported and the account at fault is named.
  • Same checks as the API: the data is encrypted again with the key of the importing user.
  • File of 2 MB at most. Together with a member's import into a family account, these are the only requests that nginx accepts above 64 KB (location ~ "^/donnees/import(-csv)?$", location ~ "^/famille/membres(/[0-9]{1,9})?$" and, for a bank statement, location ~ "^/comptes/[0-9]{1,9}/releves/fichier$"), and the only ones for which php-fpm accepts a file (var/uploads).

items.title: Family account
items.text:
The same file can be imported into a family account, for one of its two members at most:

  • Same checks as the import into an empty account (ExportReader, without a database): types, dates, months within the opening period, shares only for real estate, loans linked to a property of the file, budget validated by the domain rules. All or nothing.
  • The validated content is kept as is, encrypted with the family account's key (family_members table), apart from the account's own accounts: it cannot be changed, and a new import replaces it.
  • When read, a member's accounts get negative identifiers based on their rank (−(rank × 1,000,000 + n)), and the categories and items of their budget identifiers from rank × 1,000,000 + 1: they never mix with another member's or with the family account's.
  • The family account's export only contains its own data.

items.title: Installing on Linux
items.text: Installation from the archive of a version. For a container, see Installing with Docker. Run the commands as root. You can repeat the installation steps with the same archive without changing permissions on data in var/. For a new version, follow the update procedure.

items.title: 1. Requirements
items.text:
• Linux with systemd. The examples use the most common paths (/etc/php/8.5/fpm, php8.5-fpm service): adapt them if your distribution has others.
  • PHP 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5 (8.5 recommended), with php-fpm and the sqlite3, xml, mbstring, intl and curl extensions.
  • nginx.
  • The sqlite3, openssl, curl and tar tools.
  • HTTPS, mandatory: a reverse proxy in front of the server, or a certificate on the server (§ 6).
  • Optional: an SMTP server, for the emails (registrations, forgotten password, alerts).

items.title: 2. Installing the archive
items.text:
Download the patrimeter-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz archive and its patrimeter-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz.sha256 checksum from the page of the latest version (GitLab project, Deploy > Releases), into /tmp.

# The most recent of the archives downloaded into /tmp
ARCHIVE="$(ls /tmp/patrimeter-v*.tar.gz | sort -V | tail -n 1)"
# Checksum checked: the command prints "OK"
(cd /tmp && sha256sum -c "$(basename "$ARCHIVE").sha256")
# Extract the code as root without touching existing data or secrets
mkdir -p /srv/patrimeter
tar -xzf "$ARCHIVE" -C /srv/patrimeter --strip-components=1 --no-same-owner \
    --anchored --no-wildcards-match-slash --exclude='*/var' --exclude='*/.env.local'
# Create only the missing directories
cd /srv/patrimeter
[ -d var ] || install -d -o www-data -g www-data -m 0750 var
[ -d var/uploads ] || install -d -o www-data -g www-data -m 0700 var/uploads

Only public/ is served by nginx: do not put Patrimeter under /var/www/.

items.title: 3. Configuring
items.text:
The server's configuration and its secrets go into /srv/patrimeter/.env.local, created once:

cd /srv/patrimeter
# File created only if it does not exist: the secrets must never change
if [ ! -f .env.local ]; then
    {
        echo 'APP_ENV=prod'
        echo "APP_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
        echo "AUTH_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
        echo 'DEFAULT_URI=https://patrimeter.example.org'
        echo 'SESSION_COOKIE_NAME=__Host-patrimeter'
        echo 'TRUSTED_PROXIES=192.168.2.1'
    } > .env.local
fi
# Readable by root and php-fpm only
chown root:www-data .env.local
chmod 0640 .env.local

Then adapt in .env.local:

  • DEFAULT_URI: the public address of the site;
  • TRUSTED_PROXIES: the address of the reverse proxy (line removed without a proxy);
  • for the emails: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, SMTP_ENCRYPTION, MAIL_FROM and ADMIN_EMAIL (recipient of the alerts);
  • for a private instance: REGISTRATION_ENABLED=false if the administrator creates the accounts (the demonstration mode, DEMO_MODE, is off by default).

To change them later, and the list of the main settings: Settings.

Copy .env.local off the server (password manager): without AUTH_SECRET_KEY, every user would have to set up their authenticator app again.

items.title: 4. Database
items.text:
cd /srv/patrimeter
# Application cache, then the database
runuser -u www-data -- php bin/console cache:warmup --no-interaction
runuser -u www-data -- php bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate --no-interaction

items.title: 5. php-fpm
items.text:
A dedicated pool (php-fpm/patrimeter.conf) and the OPcache setting (php-fpm/patrimeter-opcache.ini):

# Installed PHP version
PHP=8.5
# Patrimeter's pool and OPcache setting; the default pool is not used
cp /srv/patrimeter/docs/php-fpm/patrimeter.conf "/etc/php/$PHP/fpm/pool.d/patrimeter.conf"
cp /srv/patrimeter/docs/php-fpm/patrimeter-opcache.ini "/etc/php/$PHP/fpm/conf.d/90-patrimeter.ini"
rm -f "/etc/php/$PHP/fpm/pool.d/www.conf"
# Configuration checked, then restart
"php-fpm$PHP" -t
systemctl restart "php$PHP-fpm"

items.title: 6. nginx
items.text: The virtual host serves the files of public/, passes to php-fpm only the application's addresses and limits the sign-in attempts. Access is restricted to private networks (allow directives of /etc/nginx/snippets/patrimeter-app.conf, to narrow down to your networks). Choose one of the two variants.

items.title: 6.1 Behind a reverse proxy
items.text:
The server stays on HTTP, port 80; the proxy holds the certificate.

# Common settings, sign-in limits and virtual host behind a proxy
cp /srv/patrimeter/docs/nginx/patrimeter-app.conf /etc/nginx/snippets/patrimeter-app.conf
cp /srv/patrimeter/docs/nginx/patrimeter-limits.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/patrimeter-limits.conf
cp /srv/patrimeter/docs/nginx/patrimeter-proxied.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/patrimeter.example.org.conf
# Virtual host enabled, in place of the default site
ln -sf ../sites-available/patrimeter.example.org.conf /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/patrimeter.example.org.conf
rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
# Configuration checked, then restart
nginx -t
systemctl restart nginx

The proxy passes the Host, X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For headers, and TRUSTED_PROXIES holds its address; otherwise, signing in fails. Example with nginx:

location / {
    proxy_pass http://192.168.2.10:80;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
}

items.title: 6.2 HTTPS on the server
items.text:
Put the certificate and its chain into /etc/ssl/certs/patrimeter.example.org.pem, the private key into /etc/ssl/private/patrimeter.example.org.key (readable by root only), then:

# Without a proxy: TRUSTED_PROXIES is not used
sed -i '/^TRUSTED_PROXIES=/d' /srv/patrimeter/.env.local
# Common settings, sign-in limits and virtual host over HTTPS
cp /srv/patrimeter/docs/nginx/patrimeter-app.conf /etc/nginx/snippets/patrimeter-app.conf
cp /srv/patrimeter/docs/nginx/patrimeter-limits.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/patrimeter-limits.conf
cp /srv/patrimeter/docs/nginx/patrimeter-tls.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/patrimeter.example.org.conf
# Virtual host enabled, in place of the default site
ln -sf ../sites-available/patrimeter.example.org.conf /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/patrimeter.example.org.conf
rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
# Configuration checked, then restart
nginx -t
systemctl restart nginx

items.title: 7. Services
items.text:
Scheduled tasks (purges, reminders, database upkeep), email alerts to ADMIN_EMAIL on failure, and the update command:

# Scheduled tasks and alerts
install -m 0644 /srv/patrimeter/docs/systemd/patrimeter-scheduler.service /etc/systemd/system/patrimeter-scheduler.service
install -m 0644 /srv/patrimeter/docs/systemd/patrimeter-alert@.service /etc/systemd/system/patrimeter-alert@.service
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now patrimeter-scheduler.service
# Update command (see Updating)
install -m 0755 /srv/patrimeter/docs/update/patrimeter-update.sh /usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-update

Then set up the daily backup: Backup and restore.

items.title: 8. Checking
items.text:
# Secure cookie, HSTS and content security policy, on a public page: each command prints one line
curl -sSI https://patrimeter.example.org/mot-de-passe-oublie | grep -i '^set-cookie: __Host-patrimeter=.*secure'
curl -sSI https://patrimeter.example.org/mot-de-passe-oublie | grep -i '^strict-transport-security'
curl -sSI https://patrimeter.example.org/mot-de-passe-oublie | grep -i '^content-security-policy'

If the first two print nothing, the application does not see HTTPS: check the proxy's headers and TRUSTED_PROXIES (§ 6.1).

# Installed PHP version
PHP=8.5
# The three services are running: the command answers "active" three times
systemctl is-active "php$PHP-fpm" nginx patrimeter-scheduler.service
# Test email to ADMIN_EMAIL
runuser -u www-data -- php /srv/patrimeter/bin/console app:alert 'Test'

Finally open the site: the installation wizard checks the configuration (HTTPS, address of the site, sending emails, alerts) and creates the first account, yours; you then set up your authenticator app. On error: /srv/patrimeter/var/log/ (application) and /var/log/nginx/ (web server).

items.title: 9. What next
items.text:
• Updating and rolling back.
  • Backup and restore.
  • Monitoring: health probe, metrics, check of new versions.
  • Users: the next accounts are created from the sign-in page ("Create an account", if REGISTRATION_ENABLED=true) or with runuser -u www-data -- php /srv/patrimeter/bin/console app:user:create you@example.com; app:user:list lists them with their number of accounts, list app gives every administration command.

items.title: Rotating AUTH_SECRET_KEY
items.text:
If the key may have leaked. Wealth data does not depend on it: only the secrets of the authenticator apps and the backup codes are concerned.

# Installed PHP version
PHP=8.5
# Database backup
/usr/local/sbin/patrimeter-backup
# Old key kept in AUTH_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS, new key drawn at random
cd /srv/patrimeter
sed -i '/^AUTH_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS=/d' .env.local
sed -i 's/^AUTH_SECRET_KEY=/AUTH_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS=/' .env.local
echo "AUTH_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)" >> .env.local
# Restart, then the secrets are encrypted again with the new key
systemctl restart "php$PHP-fpm" patrimeter-scheduler.service
runuser -u www-data -- php bin/console app:auth-secrets:rotate

Then ask each user to generate new backup codes (My account page), and remove the old key:

# Installed PHP version
PHP=8.5
# Old key removed, then restart
sed -i '/^AUTH_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS=/d' /srv/patrimeter/.env.local
systemctl restart "php$PHP-fpm" patrimeter-scheduler.service

Finally copy the new .env.local off the server.

items.title: Updating Patrimeter
items.text:
Before each update, read the Installation part of the CHANGELOG for each version newer than yours, and do what it asks (a new configuration variable, for example). Most of the time, there is nothing to do. The installed version is shown at the bottom of every page.

In both cases, the database is backed up automatically before any change.

items.title: 1. With Docker
items.text: See Installing with Docker, § 4: docker compose pull, then docker compose up -d.

items.title: 2. On Linux
items.text:
Download the archive of the new version and its checksum (GitLab project, Deploy > Releases) into /tmp, then, as root:

# The most recent of the archives downloaded into /tmp
ARCHIVE="$(ls /tmp/patrimeter-v*.tar.gz | sort -V | tail -n 1)"
# Backup of the database, then this version installed
patrimeter-update "$ARCHIVE"

Starting with the 3.5 updater, patrimeter-update prepares the new release before stopping the web service and scheduled tasks. It then backs up the last confirmed entry, verifies the copy, applies migrations and restarts. The copy stays with the previous release, outside backup rotation. If creating or checking it fails, the old release restarts. A rollback verifies the copy before interrupting the running site.

Then check:

# Installed PHP version
PHP=8.5
# The three services are running: the command answers "active" three times
systemctl is-active "php$PHP-fpm" nginx patrimeter-scheduler.service
# The application answers: status "pass"
curl -fsS https://patrimeter.example.org/sante

Sign in: your amounts are those from before, and the bottom of the page shows the new version.

items.title: 3. Rolling back (Linux)
items.text:
If the new version does not work:

# Previous version and database from before the update
patrimeter-update --rollback

The entries made since the update are lost.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Patrimeter's settings are variables, one per line (NAME=value), in a single file:

  • on Linux: /srv/patrimeter/.env.local (installation);
  • with Docker: patrimeter.env, next to compose.yaml (Docker).

They can be changed at any time, without touching the data. The full commented list is in .env.example.

items.title: On Linux
items.text:
# Installed PHP version
PHP=8.5
# Open the settings file and change the line you want
nano /srv/patrimeter/.env.local
# Taken into account: the site and the scheduled tasks start again with the new settings
systemctl restart "php$PHP-fpm" patrimeter-scheduler.service

items.title: With Docker
items.text:
cd /srv/patrimeter-docker
# Open the settings file and change the line you want
nano patrimeter.env
# Taken into account: the container is recreated with the new settings, the database is kept
docker compose up -d

In patrimeter.env, values are written without quotes (MAIL_FROM=Patrimeter <patrimeter@example.com>); in .env.local, a value that contains spaces goes between quotes.

items.title: Turning the demonstration mode on
items.text:
The "Try the demo" button of the sign-in page opens a temporary account, filled with example data, without registration; it is deleted after 2 hours or at sign-out. Off by default: only turn it on for an instance shown to visitors.

DEMO_MODE=true

items.title: Changing the email server
items.text:
SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_USER=patrimeter@example.com
SMTP_PASSWORD=password-of-the-smtp-account
SMTP_ENCRYPTION=starttls
MAIL_FROM="Patrimeter <patrimeter@example.com>"

SMTP_ENCRYPTION: starttls (port 587), tls (port 465) or none (local relay). After the restart, a test email is sent to ADMIN_EMAIL:

# On Linux
runuser -u www-data -- php /srv/patrimeter/bin/console app:alert 'Test'
# With Docker
docker compose exec app patrimeter-console app:alert 'Test'

items.title: 3. Main settings
items.text: Setting Default Effect DEFAULT_URI — public address of the site: links of the emails, passkeys TRUSTED_PROXIES empty address of the reverse proxy that carries HTTPS APP_TIMEZONE Europe/Paris time zone of the dates and of the current month SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, SMTP_ENCRYPTION, MAIL_FROM empty sending emails; empty SMTP_HOST: no email ADMIN_EMAIL root@localhost recipient of the server's alerts REGISTRATION_ENABLED true "Create an account" on the sign-in page REGISTRATION_ALLOWED_DOMAINS empty registrations limited to these domains (example.com,example.org) DEMO_MODE false "Try the demo" button GAMIFICATION true challenges and stars (each user can also hide them) API_ENABLED, MCP_ENABLED false REST API and MCP service for AI agents (API) CARBURE_ALLOWED_HOSTS empty Carbure instances allowed (empty: all) DOCUMENTATION_URL, DOCUMENTATION_ON_LOGIN documentation site, true link to this documentation SHOW_VERSION true version at the bottom of the pages UPDATE_CHECK_URL, UPDATE_CHECK_TOKEN empty daily check for new versions (monitoring)

items.title: 4. Not to change
items.text:
• APP_SECRET: changing it signs everyone out.
  • AUTH_SECRET_KEY: only changed with the planned procedure (rotating the key), otherwise every user would have to set up their authenticator app again.
  • SESSION_COOKIE_NAME and DATABASE_URL: set by the installation.

items.title: Monitoring
items.text:
Two addresses, without session or authentication, for a probe or a metrics collector. They give no user data; like the rest of the site, nginx only serves them to private networks (§ 8 of the installation). To restrict them to the monitoring machine, add a location ^~ /sante with its own allow directives to /etc/nginx/snippets/patrimeter-app.conf.

Address Format For /sante JSON (application/health+json, "health check" format) availability probe: Uptime Kuma, proxy monitoring… /sante/metriques Prometheus text Prometheus, Grafana Alloy, OpenTelemetry Collector

Why Prometheus rather than OpenTelemetry? The Prometheus format can be written without a library, whereas OpenTelemetry would require its SDK, a dependency to add outside Symfony. The OpenTelemetry Collector reads this format natively (prometheus receiver), and so do most tools: nothing is lost.

items.title: Checks
Metrics
items.text:
Metric Meaning patrimeter_up 1 if no check fails (the database answers) patrimeter_database_up 1 if the database answers patrimeter_database_response_seconds duration of a basic query on the database patrimeter_last_backup_timestamp_seconds Unix time of the last successful backup (0: none) patrimeter_last_maintenance_timestamp_seconds Unix time of the last run of the scheduled tasks (0: none) patrimeter_disk_free_bytes free space on the var/ disk patrimeter_update_available 1 if a more recent version is published (daily check enabled)

Timestamps rather than ages: this is the Prometheus way, the age is computed in the alerting rule.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
Prometheus:

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: patrimeter
    scheme: https
    metrics_path: /sante/metriques
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['patrimeter.example.org']

Alerting rules:

groups:
  - name: patrimeter
    rules:
      - alert: PatrimeterDown
        expr: up{job="patrimeter"} == 0 or patrimeter_up == 0
        for: 5m
      - alert: PatrimeterBackupTooOld
        expr: time() - patrimeter_last_backup_timestamp_seconds > 26 * 3600
      - alert: PatrimeterScheduledTasksStopped
        expr: time() - patrimeter_last_maintenance_timestamp_seconds > 2 * 3600
      - alert: PatrimeterDiskFull
        expr: patrimeter_disk_free_bytes < 512 * 1024 * 1024

OpenTelemetry Collector:

receivers:
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
        - job_name: patrimeter
          scheme: https
          metrics_path: /sante/metriques
          static_configs:
            - targets: ['patrimeter.example.org']

Uptime Kuma: "HTTP(s) - Json Query" probe on https://patrimeter.example.org/sante, expression status, expected value pass (or a plain HTTP probe: 503 if the database does not answer).
