items.title: Accessibility
items.text: Patrimeter aims for level AA of the WCAG 2.2 guidelines (adopted by the French RGAA). No external audit has been carried out: this page describes what is done and checked, and the known limits. Report any difficulty to the administrator of your instance.

items.title: Sight: low vision and colour blindness
items.text:
• Contrast: at least 4.5:1 for all text, 3:1 for field borders, the focus outline and graphical elements, in the light theme as in the dark theme.
  • Colour blindness: the six colours of the pyramid remain distinct from one another when simulating protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia. Above all, no information relies on colour alone:
    • each level of the pyramid shows its name, its amount and its share;
    • in the history chart, each level also has its own pattern (hatching, dots, lines…), and the table of monthly values gives the same figures;
    • increases and decreases carry their sign (+ or −), carried-over balances the "carried over" label, loans in the monthly update the "owed" label, the "−" sign and a dotted underline, input errors a written message.
  • Dark theme if you wish (button at the top of the screen), otherwise the system's theme.
  • Zoom: the page follows the browser's zoom and text size; designed for mobile first (checked at 390 pixels wide), it rearranges itself into a single column instead of scrolling sideways.
  • Screen readers: language declared, headings in order, named navigation areas, fields linked to their label, announced messages (confirmations and errors), pyramid and scales described by a text alternative, chart backed by a table.

These colour checks are automatic: a continuous integration test fails if a changed colour drops below these thresholds.

items.title: Hearing: deafness and hearing loss
items.text:
Patrimeter plays no sound, no video, no audio content: all the information is written.

  • Confirmations, warnings and errors appear on screen, as text; confirmation and reset links and administration alerts arrive by email.
  • Authentication requires no call, no voice code, no audio CAPTCHA: authenticator app (code shown), backup codes, passkeys or security keys.
  • No action is time-limited by a sound signal; the session expires after a period of inactivity, back to the sign-in page.

items.title: Keyboard and motor skills
items.text:
• Everything can be done with the keyboard; the focus is always visible (thick outline).
  • The Patrimeter logo, at the top of every page, leads back to the Net worth page. The header, the navigation and the content are marked-up areas: a screen reader goes straight to the content.
  • Input fields are 44 pixels high, except those of the monthly update, more compact to fit on a table row (at least 24 pixels, like isolated buttons and links).
  • Monthly update: Enter moves to the next field, Shift + Enter to the previous one, Esc restores the suggested amount (monthly update).
  • Chart animations are turned off if the system asks to reduce motion.

items.title: Known limits
items.text:
• The history chart is an image for screen readers: its content is in the table placed below it.
  • The interface and this documentation exist in French and in English; the technical pages about developing Patrimeter (architecture, continuous integration…) only exist in French.

items.title: API and assistants (MCP)
items.text:
Patrimeter offers a REST API and an MCP service (for an assistant such as Claude) with the same authentication as the site:

  • personal token, created in My account, "AI agents" tab (read only, or read and write, limited lifetime);
  • or access granted to an application, after signing in and consenting in the browser (OAuth 2.1).

Each access can be revoked from the same tab, which also gives the addresses of the MCP service and of the API to give to the AI agent (account menu, AI agents), each with a Copy button that puts it in the clipboard. An assistant that calls these tools sends your data to its provider: the consent covers this too.

The rate is limited per token: 120 requests in a row, then one per second.

The API and the MCP service are disabled by default: the instance administrator enables each of them with the API_ENABLED and MCP_ENABLED variables (API and MCP). As long as neither is enabled, the "AI agents" tab does not appear in My account, nor in the account menu.

Complete reference (addresses, MCP tools, examples): API and MCP. Each API operation, its parameters and its responses: API reference, generated from the OpenAPI description (openapi.yaml).

items.title: Real estate
items.text: Real estate tab of My account: one table per property, laid out like the list of accounts. The property first, with your share of its value and the value counted for you, then its loans (each one with the way it is counted and its outstanding principal), each with its status (entered or carried over); at the bottom, its net value, the one the pyramid counts. The name of a property or of a loan opens its page. Properties (main residence, rental, SCPI, SCI…) are only created here, with their share and their loans; the account form does not offer them.

items.title: Creating a property and its loans
items.text:
New property creates the property and its loans in one go:

  • Type: main residence, second home, furnished (LMNP) or unfurnished rental, SCPI, SCI, SIIC. A click on the field (or on its arrow) shows the whole list; type to keep only the types that contain the text ("scpi", "rental"…), ignoring case and accents. A second home counts in the Real estate level of the pyramid, and its loans are second home mortgages;
  • Total value of the property: the value of the whole property, even if you only own part of it;
  • Your share (%): 100% by default, 50% for a property owned by two…
  • Loans: name and outstanding principal of each one; Add a loan for one more loan.

items.title: Share and loans
items.text:
Each linked loan is counted in one of two ways:

The amount entered is Counted the total, counted according to my share (prorata) outstanding principal × your share of the property my own share as is

Example: a €200,000 property owned at 50%, a joint loan of €100,000 (prorata) and a personal loan of €10,000 (your share):

  • value counted: 200,000 × 50% = €100,000;
  • loans: 100,000 × 50% + 10,000 = €60,000;
  • net value for you: €40,000.

The share can change over time (buying a share, donation): on the property's page, Your share of the property records a new share from a given month. An existing loan is linked to a property from its own page (Financed property).

items.title: Household budget
items.text:
Budget menu: the household's monthly budget. Each adult's income first pays the shared budget (housing, everyday life, leisure and household savings), paid into the joint account. Each person then pays their own expenses and savings from what they have left. The budget is read alongside the net worth of the same month and compared with the 50/30/20 rule: 50% of income for needs, 30% for wants, 20% for savings.

A single Patrimeter account manages the whole household: you enter everyone's income and expenses, your partner does not need to sign in.

items.title: Creating the budget
items.text:
On the first visit, Patrimeter asks for:

  • Number of adults (one or two) and Number of children (none to 12), in two lists: the form then only shows the rows of these people;
  • for each adult and each child, their first name and their year of birth, picked from a calendar of years. A budget item can be assigned to a child: the budget then shows what each one costs. A child of working age (16 in the year) can have incomes of their own;
  • Emergency savings target, in months of household expenses (often 3 to 6; 0: no target).

Create the budget suggests categories and their items, to rename, add to or delete:

Category Group Suggested items Housing needs rent or mortgage, service charges, insurance, energy, internet and phone Everyday life needs groceries, health, transport Leisure wants outings and restaurants, subscriptions, gifts Household savings savings emergency savings, holiday fund, home improvement fund Personal expenses (each adult) needs phone, transport Personal leisure (each adult) wants outings, sport Personal savings (each adult) savings savings account, share savings plan

items.title: Entering the month's amounts
items.text:
Edit the … budget, or the Budget part of the Monthly update menu, opens the month's budget entry:

  • Income for the month: each adult's net income, and that of each child who is 16 or more in the year (a summer job, an apprenticeship…), added to the household's income;
  • Splitting the joint account (couple): in proportion to the month's income, or fixed share (for example, the first adult pays 27.5%, the second the rest);
  • the amount of each item, category by category: shared budget, then each adult's own budget. An empty field counts as 0.

Category totals, the payment into the joint account and what the household has left are worked out as you type; Enter moves to the next item. Amounts are read in the language of the page, as in the monthly update.

The amounts saved for a month apply to the following months until you change them: a month without an entry takes the budget of an earlier month, marked carried over. To change the budget from a given month (pay rise, new loan…), edit the budget of that month. Delete the … amounts restores those of an earlier month.

At the top of the entry, Copy the budget of another month fills the form with the amounts in force in the chosen month picked from the calendar: check them, then save; nothing is saved before. The same box leads to adding an item or a category (tax household and categories) and an account, and Update my tax household opens the tax household (adults, children, emergency savings target) in My account. Next month's budget can be prepared in advance.

As long as the tax household does not exist, the Budget part of the monthly update says so (No budget yet) with a single button, Create my tax household, which leads to the creation of the budget.

items.title: Reading the budget
items.text:
• Summary: savings rate (planned savings as a share of income), possible rate (adding what is left available), household income, expenses (needs and wants), savings and what is left available (or the overspend if the budget exceeds income); net worth for the month, with a link to the Net worth page.
  • Budget flows: from each adult's income to the household budget, then to needs, wants, savings and available, with their share of income and their target, then to the categories. The width of a flow is proportional to its amount. On a phone, the chart scrolls horizontally.
  • 50/30/20 rule: each group's share of income, and the line of its target.
  • Joint account: each adult's payment. In proportion to income, the first adult's share is rounded to the nearest cent; the second pays the rest, so the two payments always add up to the total.
  • What each person has left: income, minus the payment into the joint account, minus their own expenses and savings.
  • Shared budget and each adult's own budget: the detail of categories and items, to expand (the ▸ arrow before the title turns when the detail is open).
  • Cost of the children: the total of the items assigned to each child; the section only appears once an item is assigned to a child of the household.

Example: a couple earns €1,860 and €4,143; the shared budget is €4,554.74, split with a fixed share of 27.5%.

First adult Second adult Income €1,860.00 €4,143.00 Joint account (27.5% / 72.5%) − €1,252.55 − €3,302.19 Own expenses and savings − €592.30 − €836.00 Left €15.15 €4.81

items.title: Budget trends
items.text: Under the 50/30/20 rule, Budget trends gives the average per month of the planned spending (needs and wants) and savings over 3, 6 and 12 months up to the month shown, and below it the same average over the period before: do you spend more than before, save less? One row per period, Expenses and Savings columns. A period going back before the first budget entered stays empty.

items.title: With your net worth
items.text:
A month's budget is compared with the net worth of the same month:

  • Key figures: net worth for the month (and its change since the previous month), emergency savings (in months of expenses), expenses of the month (needs and wants, savings excluded);
  • Emergency savings: the pyramid level, compared with the household's monthly expenses, on a gauge in months of expenses (the same as in the recommendations of the Net worth page): zones below one month, below the target and up to twice the target, a line for the target, and a finding (Alert, Warning with the missing amount, Good, or Note above twice the target);
  • Savings payments: a savings item linked to its account (savings account, share savings plan…) shows two bars, its planned payment and the change in the account's balance over the month (this month's statement minus the previous month's), then a finding: payment reached, less than planned (with the gap), balance down, or month's statement to enter. This change also includes interest, gains and withdrawals: it is a benchmark;
  • Net worth for the month, also at the top of the budget.

items.title: Actual spending with Carbure
items.text: Linked to your Carbure instance, the budget compares every month the planned amount of each category with the actual spending of your bank accounts.

items.title: Tax household and categories
items.text:
The Tax household and categories page, a tab of My account, also opened by the Set up tax household and categories button at the top of the Budget page, organises the budget:

  • Tax household: the same lists of the number of adults and of children, then each one with their year of birth. Lowering the number of children removes the last ones of the list; clearing a child's first name removes them from the household, and their items are no longer assigned to them. A child keeps their items when their first name changes. A household created before version 2.26 asks for the missing years at its next save. Emergency savings target. A second adult who joins the household receives the suggested categories; an adult can only leave the household once their own categories have been deleted or moved to the shared budget;
  • Categories: name, group of the 50/30/20 rule (needs, wants, savings) and who pays it (the joint account, or an adult from what they have left);
  • Items: Add under a category; an item's name opens its page: category, optional child and, for a savings item, the account receiving the payment.

The ↑ and ↓ arrows change the order: a category among those of the same budget (shared or one adult's), an item within its category. The budget and its entry follow this order.

Deleting a category deletes its items; deleting an item removes its amount from every month.

items.title: Privacy
items.text: The budget is encrypted with your key, like your accounts: first names, names of categories and items, income and amounts. It is part of the export of your data.

items.title: Carbure: actual versus planned
items.text: Carbure is a free, self-hosted spending tracker: it fetches your bank transactions and sorts them into categories. Linked to your Carbure instance, Patrimeter reads each month's actual spending and compares it with the planned budget.

items.title: Linking your instance
items.text:
1. In Carbure, the administrator enables the MCP server (it is disabled by default).
  2. In Carbure, create an API token: Settings, API tokens, Create. A limited lifetime (90 days, one year) is better. The token starts with cbt_; it is shown only once.
  3. In Patrimeter, My account, Carbure tab: the address of your instance (for example https://carbure.maison.lan) and the token, then Link Carbure. The address of the MCP service that Carbure shows (https://carbure.maison.lan/api/mcp) will do too.

Patrimeter then reads your expense categories: the page shows how many. Each user links their own instance; the token is encrypted with your key and never shown again (only its last four characters). To change the address without changing the token, leave the token field empty.

items.title: Mapping the categories
items.text: Each top-level Carbure expense category (its subcategories included) counts towards one budget category, or is ignored. Categories with the same name are mapped automatically; the others are chosen in Category mapping. Carbure's income categories are not used.

items.title: Planned and actual
items.text:
The budget page adds the Planned and actual section: for each mapped category, the planned amount, the month's actual spending in Carbure and the gap (actual minus planned: when positive, spending exceeds the budget), with two bars. Spending in categories without a mapping is flagged, with a link to map them.

If Carbure does not answer, refuses the token or has not enabled its MCP server, the budget says so and is shown anyway. The message tells a refused token (to create again in Carbure) apart from an address without a Carbure MCP service (wrong address, or MCP server disabled).

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Patrimeter only calls the …/api/mcp address of your instance, read-only, without following redirects, with a limited delay and response size; it never sends back what it reads there.
  • Calls are limited per user (a burst of 30, then one every 10 seconds).
  • The Patrimeter administrator can restrict the allowed instances (CARBURE_ALLOWED_HOSTS, see the installation).
  • Delete the link erases the address, the token and the mapping from Patrimeter; revoke the token in Carbure too.

items.title: Accounts and loans
items.text:
An account is something you own (current account, savings account, life insurance, PEA…), a loan something you owe (mortgage, consumer loan…). Accounts tab of My account (account menu, My profile). Properties have their own tab, Real estate: they are created there, with your share and their loans (real estate). To create many accounts, properties and loans in one go, from a spreadsheet: CSV import.

The list shows your accounts like the monthly update: one table per level of the pyramid, with for each account its type, its status (entered this month, or carried over: last known balance) and its balance for the month. A loan is marked owed, with its outstanding principal preceded by "−". An account's name opens its page.

Changing the opening date cannot put an existing statement before the account’s first active month.

items.title: Creating an account
items.text:
+ New account, then:

Field Purpose Name What you call it ("Marie's Livret A") Type Predefined types; the type suggests the level and the nature. In the Alternative level, tangible assets: gold, silver and other precious metals, jewellery, watches, works of art and collectibles, wines and spirits, car, motorbike (enter their estimated resale value). A click on the field (or on its arrow) shows the whole list; type to keep only the types that contain the text ("livret", "pea", "mortgage"…), ignoring case and accents; arrows and Enter to choose with the keyboard Pyramid level Main residence, emergency savings, guaranteed funds, equities, real estate, alternative Asset or liability Asset (account, investment, property) or liability (loan, debt) Opening date The account counts from this month on Current balance Optional: balance for the current month

For a loan, enter the outstanding principal, as a positive amount: Patrimeter subtracts it from the level.

items.title: Balances
items.text: An account's page recalls its type, its level, whether it is an asset or a liability and its opening date, then lists its balances month by month; Add or correct a balance enters or corrects a past month. The month is picked from the calendar, as at the top of the pages. The usual monthly entry is rather done in the monthly update, for all accounts at once.

items.title: Reading a bank statement
items.text:
Rather than copying a balance, Or read the balance of a bank statement takes the file your bank exports for this account, in OFX (or QFX) or CAMT.053 (ISO 20022) format: Patrimeter reads its closing balance and its date, then fills in the month and the amount of the form. Check them, then Add or correct a balance: nothing is saved before. For a loan, the negative balance of the statement becomes the capital owed.

The QIF and CSV files of the banks give the transactions, without the balance: export an OFX or CAMT.053 statement instead (most banks offer them where you download your transactions). A file in a foreign currency, or that holds several accounts, is refused with a message that says what to do.

items.title: Closing, reactivating, deleting
items.text:
• Archive with a closing date: the account no longer counts from the following month on; its history stays.
  • Reactivate an archived account.
  • Delete permanently: the account and all its balances disappear, including from the history.

items.title: Challenges and stars
items.text:
Challenges menu of the main bar: stars for good habits (entering your balances every month, keeping your budget, holding emergency savings, moving towards your goals, protecting your account), a level that rises with them and a saver profile. Nothing more to enter: everything is computed from your data.

Not investment advice. Indicative benchmarks, to adapt to your situation: this is not investment advice. No challenge rewards a return, the share of shares or cryptocurrencies, a product or more risk, and Patrimeter never compares you with the other users.

items.title: The Challenges page
items.text:
At the top, My level and My profile give your two statuses; each leads to its card. Then come:

  • My stars: the total, on a dial, and Where do my stars come from?, the stars earned by family of challenges (first steps, balance entries, budget and goals, cushion and credit, account security);
  • My level: where you stand between your level and the next one, and how many stars are missing; See the 6 levels unfolds the ladder;
  • My profile: your stage, the next one, a bar when its condition can be counted (months entered, months of spending set aside…) and what it asks; See the 5 stages unfolds the ladder;
  • My streak: the months entered in a row and the joker of the year.

items.title: The challenges
items.text:
Each challenge gives up to three stars, at thresholds (five for First steps, two for Protected account):

Challenge One star Two stars Three stars First steps one star per step done, five in all (see below) Entry streak 3 months in a row 6 months in a row 12 months in a row Wealth up to date 1 month where every account has its balance entered 6 months 12 months Safety cushion 1 month of spending set aside half of your target your target No consumer loan 1 month without consumer loan 6 months in a row 12 months in a row Goal under way 25% of your most advanced goal 50% 75% Budget kept up to date 1 month of budget entered 3 months 6 months Protected account a passkey a second one, as a spare Savings rate kept 1 month at the rate you aim at 3 months in a row 6 months in a row
  • A month counts in the streak as soon as at least one balance is entered in it (not only carried over). As long as the current month is not entered, the streak goes on from the previous month. One forgotten month per calendar year is forgiven (the joker), if it follows an entered month: the page says whether the joker of the year is still available.
  • The safety cushion is measured in months of spending (needs and wants) of the budget, and the target is the tax household's (6 months by default). Without household nor budget, the challenge says so.
  • The goal under way follows your most advanced savings goal. Without any goal, the challenge says so.
  • The savings rate kept counts the months in a row where the budget in force plans savings of at least the rate you choose on its card (from 5% to 50%): Patrimeter suggests none. Without a rate chosen, nor a budget, the challenge says so. A month without a budget entered takes the previous month's, as in the budget.

Each card shows its score ("1 star earned out of 3"), then its thresholds from left to right, each under its star: Earned (full star), Next (circled star) or Later. Then come Already done (where you stand this month) and what is missing for the next star, for example "For the 2nd star: 3 more months entered in a row."; a challenge that must first be made measurable says what to do (Before you start). Rule of the challenge unfolds what it rewards. The challenges whose stars are all earned move to Completed, marked Challenge completed.

A star earned is never lost: if a streak stops or a balance goes down, the stars already obtained stay; only the progress of the month changes.

items.title: Stars after the monthly entry
items.text: After Save … balances in the monthly entry, a message announces the new highest score for each challenge, for example “New star, challenge ‘Entry streak’: 1 of 3.” Checking the dashboard, Challenges page or API first does not dismiss the announcement. Saving the same balances again does not repeat it. If you turn challenges off, you can still save balances without star announcements. Your stars and any pending announcements are kept for when you turn challenges back on.

items.title: Level
items.text: The total of the stars gives a level, from 1 to 6: Curious (from the start), Attentive (4 stars), Steady (8), Far-sighted (13), Consistent (18) and Master of the pyramid (24). In all, 28 stars are possible: the Challenges page shows "8 stars of 28" at the top, and the ladder of the six levels, from the first to the last, with yours (you are here) and what is missing for the next one.

items.title: Saver profile
items.text:
The stage is computed every month; it is the highest rung whose condition is met, along with those of every rung below:

  1. Discovery: a first month entered;
  2. Organized: three months where every account has its balance entered;
  3. Protected: emergency savings reaching your target, in months of the budget's spending;
  4. Serene: no consumer loan to repay;
  5. Builder: a savings goal reached and twelve months of entries in a row.

The style, optional, is chosen in My profile, Challenges and stars section: Ant (a little every month), Project (a dated project), Home (the home and its loan first) or Horizon (the long term). It only changes the order of the challenges shown; it says nothing about what you should buy nor about the risk to take. The profile is not a risk profile test.

items.title: "First steps" card
items.text: On the Net worth page, as long as the five first steps have not been done once, a card lists them with a link to each: describe your household, create your accounts, enter the month's balances, add your home or a property, set a first savings goal. Each step is worth a star, counted as soon as the card is shown. As long as you have not chosen a saver style, the card offers it. Hide this card removes it; the Challenges page brings it back.

items.title: AI agents
items.text: The challenges can also be read through the API and the MCP service (GET /api/v1/challenges, get_challenges tool), with the same notice: this is not investment advice.

items.title: Turning the challenges off
items.text:
Challenge settings, at the bottom of the Challenges page, or My account > My profile, Challenges and stars section: Turn off challenges and stars removes the page from the navigation, the "First steps" card and the messages after the entry. Your stars are kept; Turn on challenges and stars brings them back.

The administrator can also remove them for the whole instance (GAMIFICATION=false, installation).

items.title: Exporting and importing your data
items.text: Your data page, from My account: to move to another Patrimeter instance, or to keep a copy of your data.

items.title: Exporting
items.text:
Download my data, after confirming your identity: a JSON file contains your accounts and loans, their balances, the shares of your properties, the links between properties and loans, and the household budget (household, categories, items and the amounts of each month).

The file is not encrypted: keep it somewhere safe and delete it after use.

Your user account (address, password, second factor, passkeys, API tokens) is not exported: it is created again on the other instance.

items.title: Family account
items.text: The same file is used by the family account: exported every month, it is imported for you by the family account, in Family members, where it replaces the previous import. The family account only keeps what the file contains, encrypted with its own key.

items.title: Creating accounts from a CSV file
items.text: To enter your accounts, loans and properties in one go, from a spreadsheet: Download the model (CSV), fill it in (one line per account), then Create the accounts. The accounts are added to the existing ones; all or nothing. Format, columns and type codes: CSV import.

items.title: Importing
items.text:
On the other instance, create your account, then Your data → Import with the file:

  • the import is done into an account that is still empty;
  • all or nothing: at the slightest problem, nothing is imported, and the account at fault is named;
  • file of 2 MB at most.

Detailed format of the file: export and import.

items.title: Family account
items.text: A family account brings together the net worth and the budget of a couple, each keeping their own account: each person enters their data on their side, exports it every month, and the family account imports it. The Net worth page (with its history), the Budget page and the report then show the family, or each person.

items.title: Setting up
items.text:
1. Each person creates their Patrimeter account and enters their accounts, their balances and, if they wish, their budget.
  2. Create a third account, for the family (another email address).
  3. In this account, open Family members (Bring a family together on the welcome Net worth page, or the Your data page), then Add a member: their name and their export file. As long as no member is imported, the page starts with the three monthly steps.

A family account brings together two members at most.

items.title: What is shared: each person's share
items.text:
The family adds up its members' data: so that nothing is counted twice, each person enters their share of what is shared.

Shared What each person enters Joint account half of its balance (or their share) House bought together the property with its share (50%…) and its linked loan, pro rata (see Real estate) Rent, groceries, bills their share of each expense, in their budget

The family account can also have its own accounts, the children's for example: they count in the family.

items.title: Every month
items.text:
1. Each person downloads their data: My profile, Export or import, then Download my data.
  2. In the family account, Family members: on each member's card, choose or drop their new file, then Update; it replaces the previous import.

At the top, the page says how many members are up to date for the month ("1 member up to date out of 2 for November 2026"). Each card carries the member's status, in words: Up to date, or To update when their file is from a previous month; it also gives their net worth, the date of the file, the date of the import and the number of accounts. More actions, then Remove … from the family, deletes their imported data from the family account, never from their own account.

items.title: Family views
items.text:
As soon as a member is imported, the Net worth page, the report to share and the budget offer a choice at the top of the page:

  • Whole family (by default): the members' accounts and the family account's own; the budget brings together the members' budgets;
  • one member: their data only, as they see it in their account;
  • Family's accounts: the family account's own accounts, the children's for example, if it has any.

A line under the choice recalls what the view adds up, and flags each member whose file is to update ("Julien's file to update", with a link to the members). In these views, the balances are counted "of the month" or "carried over": they come from the members' files, not from an entry in the family account.

The choice is kept from one page to the next. In the family:

  • imported accounts carry the name of their member ("Savings account · Alex") and cannot be changed;
  • the budget is read-only: each member becomes an adult, with their income and all their categories; there is no joint account to split, since each person entered their share. Children with the same first name are brought together, and their cost adds up both budgets; the emergency savings target is the higher of the two;
  • the Net worth page recommendations compare the family's emergency savings with the family's expenses.

items.title: Privacy
items.text:
• Imported data is encrypted with the family account's key, like all wealth data: the server administrator cannot read it.
  • The export file is not encrypted: delete it once imported.
  • The family account's export only contains its own data, not its members'.

items.title: CSV import
items.text: To create your accounts, loans and properties in one go, without entering them one by one: a CSV file, written with a spreadsheet (LibreOffice Calc, Excel, Numbers…) or by hand, one line per account. Your data page, from My account, Create accounts from a CSV file section.

items.title: In short
items.text:
1. Download the model (CSV): a file ready to fill in, with a savings account, a property and its loan as examples.
  2. Replace the examples with your accounts, one line each, and save in CSV format.
  3. Create the accounts with this file: you land on the list of accounts, which shows them.

The accounts are added to the existing ones. All or nothing: at the slightest refusal, nothing is created, and the message gives the line concerned (line 1 is that of the columns, as in the spreadsheet). File of 1 MB and 500 accounts at most.

items.title: Example
items.text:
name,type,opened_on,balance,month,level,nature,share,property,loan_mode,closed_on
Savings account,livret_a,2020-01-15,12345.67,,,,,,,
Flat in Lyon,location_nue,2018-06-01,250000,,,,50,,,
Flat loan,credit_immo_locatif,2018-06-01,180000,,,,,Flat in Lyon,prorata,
Old PEL,pel_cel,2012-09-01,5000,2019-12,,,,,,2020-01-31

Only the name, type and opened_on columns are required; the others may be missing, in any order. An empty cell means "not given".

items.text:

For a loan, the outstanding principal, positive. For a property, its total value, even if you only own a share of it month mois no Month of the balance: YYYY-MM (2026-10) or MM/YYYY (10/2026). Empty: the current month (or the opening month, if it is to come) level niveau no Level of the pyramid, if it is not that of the type: residence, precaution, fonds_euros, actions, immobilier or exotique nature nature no asset or liability (actif, passif), if it is not that of the type share part no For a property: your share as a percentage (50, 33.3333), from the opening month. Empty: 100% property bien no For a loan: the name of the property it finances, in the file or among your properties already entered loan_mode mode_credit no For a loan linked to a property: prorata (the amount is that of the whole loan, counted according to your share of the property) or own (the amount is already your share); empty: prorata. See properties closed_on cloture no Closing date of a closed account (YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY): it is created then archived

Column names accept capitals, accents and spaces ("Closed on", "Mode crédit"). An unknown column is refused, so that a typo does not go unnoticed.

One balance per account: the history of the previous months is entered afterwards, in the monthly update or the account's page.

items.title: Saving the file
items.text:
• Separator: semicolon (the choice of a spreadsheet in French), comma or tab; Patrimeter recognizes that of the line of the columns. A value that contains the separator is written between quotes ("Savings, joint").
  • Encoding: UTF-8, with or without BOM, or Windows-1252 (the "CSV" of Excel in French); accents go through in both cases.
  • Dates and months: a spreadsheet sometimes turns 2026-10 into a date ("Oct-26"); set these columns to the Text format before filling them in, or write 10/2026.
  • LibreOffice Calc: File > Save As, type "Text CSV", tick "Edit filter settings", character set Unicode (UTF-8), separator ,.
  • Excel: File > Save As, type "CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited)".

items.title: Properties and loans
items.text: A property is an asset of the Main residence or Real estate level (types marked property below): its share column gives your share. A loan (liability nature) is attached to its property by the property column, which repeats the property's name, whether the property comes before or after it in the file, or is already entered in Patrimeter. The properties and loans created this way appear in the Real estate tab, as if they had been entered with New property.

items.title: Indicators
items.text: An indicator is a total you define yourself: pyramid levels and chosen accounts, followed every month as the net worth. For instance, "Retirement": the Shares level and a life insurance; or "Available savings": the emergency savings and a securities account.

items.title: Creating an indicator
items.text:
On the Net worth page, Indicators, then New indicator:

Field Content Name 60 characters at most Pyramid levels The net total of each ticked level (assets minus loans) Accounts The ticked accounts; an account that already belongs to a ticked level is counted once Also show its share of the net worth The percentage of the net worth that the indicator represents

At least one level or one account is needed; 10 indicators at most.

items.title: Following your indicators
items.text:
• The Indicators page gives the value of each one this month and its change over a month.
  • The Net worth page shows them in the My indicators box, for the month displayed.
  • The name of an indicator opens its page: its last twelve months, the change and the deletion.

The values are worked out as the net worth: ownership shares and linked loans included, a month without a balance carrying over the previous one. Like your other data, the indicators are encrypted and are part of the export.

items.title: Savings goals
items.text: Goals menu of the main bar, between Budget and Monthly update: an amount to reach by a date, and every month, Patrimeter tells you whether you are on track. Nothing more to enter: the follow-up is computed from your monthly balances.

items.title: Setting a goal
items.text:
Goals are created and changed in Monthly update, Goals tab: New goal, or a goal's name to change or delete it.

New goal:

  • Name: "Down payment for the house", "Emergency fund"…;
  • Target (list): an amount, or months of budget spending (for instance 6 months for an emergency fund): the amount then follows each month the spending (needs and wants) of the budget. The next field depends on this choice: Amount to reach, or Number of months of spending;
  • Start month: this month by default, or a past month for a goal already under way (for instance savings begun in January);
  • To reach by: a month after the start month, and to come;
  • What the goal measures (list):
    • the whole net worth;
    • one level of the pyramid (for instance emergency savings): the Pyramid level list appears;
    • chosen accounts (for instance the Livret A and the LDDS): the list of Accounts to tick appears. A loan ticked counts negatively.

Only the fields useful to the choice made are shown; without JavaScript, all of them are shown, each with the case it is for.

The starting point is the value measured in the start month: it fixes the trajectory. It does not change if you then change the target or the date; it is computed again if you change the start month or what the goal measures. Twenty goals at most.

items.title: On track or off track?
items.text:
Every month, for each goal:

  • the effort needed: what is missing, divided by the months left ("you need to set aside €450 a month until November 2027");
  • the pace observed: the average progress of the last six months (fewer if the goal is more recent). An average smooths the ups and downs of the stock market;
  • the status, always written in words:
Status When Reached the amount is reached Ahead the pace exceeds the effort needed by at least 20 % On track the pace covers the effort needed To watch the pace covers between 80 % and 100 % of the effort Behind the pace covers less than 80 % of the effort, or the date has passed Too early to tell the goal dates from this month: the pace is measured from the next month

If more is needed, Patrimeter tells what is missing each month and the month the goal would be reached at this pace. If savings items of the budget go to the goal's accounts, it also compares the planned savings with the effort needed.

On the Goals page, each goal reads as follows:

  • a ring gives the share of the target reached ("72% reached"); a mark on the ring shows where the planned trajectory should put you this month: a ring going past the mark is ahead, one falling short of it is behind;
  • the status as a pill, next to the name;
  • tiles for the key figures: current amount, target and its month, effort needed and pace observed per month;
  • a chart from the start to the target month: what is reached (solid line over a coloured area), the planned trajectory (dashes), the projection at the current pace (dots) and the target (thin line). On hover or touch, a bubble gives the amounts of the month. Under the chart, a sentence repeats the figures (screen readers, pages without JavaScript);
  • the status of the last months.

items.title: Where to see it
items.text:
• Goals page (main bar): each goal, its status, its chart and its last months.
  • After the monthly entry: a message for each goal whose status changes ("Goal "Down payment": Behind → On track").

Goals are encrypted like the rest of your data, and are part of the export. As the server cannot read your data outside your session, no report is sent by email: the follow-up is looked at in the application.

items.title: Trying without an account
items.text:
If the instance offers the demo, the sign-in page shows Try the demo: Patrimeter opens a temporary account at once, without registration or code, filled with fictitious data (three years of wealth, a household budget). A banner reminds you when it will be deleted: after 2 hours, or as soon as you sign out, with everything you entered in it. The security settings, the import, the family account and Carbure are not available in it, and the amount of data is limited. Do not enter any real data in it. The My account menu leads to the accounts and the properties: you can add some. If too many demo accounts have just been created, the sign-in page tells how long to wait.

A guided tour starts at once: a card at the bottom of the screen presents, in thirteen steps, the net worth, the savings goals, the pyramid, the monthly entry, the accounts, the properties, the budget and the report, and outlines the element it talks about. Next and Previous go from one step to another, changing page if needed; Stop the tour closes it. The banner at the top starts it again (Start the guided tour) or, if you left it for another page, resumes it at the step you had reached.

items.title: Creating your account
items.text:
On the sign-in page, Create an account: email address and password (at least 12 characters, hard to guess; a sentence of several words works). A password found in a known leak is refused.

While you type, under the password, a bar and a label show its strength (from Very weak to Very strong), estimated the way the server does: at least Fair is required. Each requirement is ticked (✓) or crossed (✗) as you type: at least 12 characters, without your email address, unpredictable enough, and both entries the same. The search in known leaks happens when you send the form, anonymously. The same indicator comes with the password change (My account) and the password reset.

The next page shows the address you entered: check it. A confirmation email arrives there; its link is valid for 24 hours and asks for the chosen password; without confirmation, the registration is erased after these 24 hours (just start again). If this address already has an account, the email simply tells you so: sign in with your usual password. If registrations are closed on your instance, the administrator creates the account for you.

items.title: Authenticator app
items.text:
The first start has four steps, recalled at the top of each screen ("Step 2 of 4 · about 2 minutes"): your account, security (authenticator app and backup codes), the recovery key, then your first accounts.

At the first sign-in, Patrimeter asks you to set up an authenticator app (mandatory second factor), on the Protect your account screen: scan the QR code, then enter the 6-digit code it shows and Enable and see my backup codes. Patrimeter then shows ten backup codes, each usable once: write them down somewhere safe, they replace the phone if it is lost. Copy the codes puts them in the clipboard, one per line, to paste them into a password manager; Print prints them.

Then, at every sign-in: address and password, then the code from the app (or a backup code).

items.title: Recovery key
items.text: Patrimeter shows a recovery key, only once, and asks you to type part of it again. Why two secrets? recalls the role of each: the backup codes replace the phone to sign in, the key opens your data again if you forget your password. Print prints the key. Your data is encrypted with a key that only your password opens: without a recovery key, a forgotten password means losing the data (access to the account, however, can be restored). Keep it with your backup codes, for example in a password manager: Copy the key puts it in the clipboard.

items.title: Unlocking
items.text: After signing in with a passkey that does not unlock, Patrimeter asks for your password to open your data: this is the Unlock screen.

items.title: Current month
items.text: In the middle of the top bar, Patrimeter shows the current month ("November 2026", "Nov 2026" on a phone), whatever the month shown by the page: it is the one the monthly update offers first. A click on it goes back to it: on the same page for the net worth, the report, the monthly update and the budget, otherwise on the Net worth page. On its own, a month is written with a capital in French too ("Novembre 2026"); within a sentence, French keeps the lower case.

items.title: Menus
items.text: At the top on a computer, at the bottom on a phone: Net worth, Budget, Goals, Challenges (challenges and stars, unless you turned them off), then, always put forward on the right, Monthly update. Your Accounts and your Real estate open from the Net worth page (buttons at the top), your Tax household and categories from the Budget page. My account, on the right, gathers the profile, the security and the AI agents.

items.title: First accounts
items.text:
As long as no account exists, the Net worth page stays on the current month and offers, as the last step of the first start, to draw your pyramid (Let's draw your pyramid):

  • Answer a few questions (recommended): one question at a time, in everyday words ("Do you have money put aside, available right away?"), answered by a range ("from €1,000 to €5,000"), an exact amount or "No, or I don't know". Why this question? says which level of the pyramid it is about. A range counts for its middle. The last question, optional, chooses your saver style (challenges). Create my accounts creates the accounts answered at once;
  • Build my pyramid, if you know your accounts: the empty pyramid, and its six levels from the base to the top. Fill opens a level with its common accounts (current account, Livret A, LDDS, LEP, PEA, life insurance…): enter today's balance of what you hold, leave the rest empty, then Confirm this level; the level takes its colour in the pyramid. I have none goes on to the next one;
  • Other ways to start, folded:
    • Express entry: all these accounts on a single page, created at once with Create my accounts;
    • Import a CSV file: accounts, loans and properties from a spreadsheet (CSV import);
    • Create account by account, with every setting: level, nature, opening date (accounts).

A family account is not filled in: under Is this account for a family?, Bring a family together leads to the family members.

The name of each account repeats its type and can be changed. For a loan, enter the outstanding principal. Approximate amounts are enough: they are marked to refine in the monthly entry, until you save them there. The accounts are opened this month, with this balance; if a line is wrong, nothing is created and the page says so. Several accounts of the same type, or a property with your share and its linked loans: add them afterwards from the Net worth page (Accounts, Real estate).

Then, the First steps card guides you until you see your whole net worth (challenges and stars). If the challenges are turned off, a Complete your net worth box offers what is still missing, a property or an account, until both exist.

items.title: Theme
items.text: The button at the top of every page switches between the light and dark themes; without a choice, the system theme applies.

items.title: Language
items.text: Patrimeter is shown in French or English: by default in your browser's language (French for any other language). The language button, next to the theme button, shows the current language (FR or EN); click it to choose Français or English from the menu. This choice is remembered on this device. Amounts follow the language: 1 234,56 € in French, €1,234.56 in English. Emails are written in the language of the page that triggered them.

items.title: Frequently asked questions
items.text:
Do I have to enter every account every month? No: an account without a balance keeps its last known balance (carried over). Enter what changes.

How do I enter a loan? Like an account whose nature is liability, with the outstanding principal as a positive amount: Patrimeter subtracts it.

I forgot my password. "Forgotten your password?" link; with your recovery key, you keep your data (security).

I lost my phone. Sign in with a backup code, then change app in My account.

Can the administrator see my amounts? No: they are encrypted with a key that only your password (or your recovery key) opens. The administrator can, however, see your address, the number of your accounts and the months entered, and the sign-in log (application security).

Can I change server? Yes: export your data, then import it on the new instance.

Can the site be used without JavaScript? Yes: every screen works without JavaScript, which only adds comfort (chart, month calendars, type lists you can type into).

Which version of Patrimeter is installed? It is shown at the bottom of every page, sign-in page included ("Patrimeter, version X.Y.Z").

I started Patrimeter in November: how do I enter the months before? Go to the month you want, then Copy balances from another month from November: the accounts opened since are included, and saving moves their opening date back (monthly update).

After an update, the screen has not changed. Reload the page, bypassing the browser cache (Ctrl+Shift+R). If nothing changes, the administrator checks the server's update (checking the update).

How do I switch to French? Click the language button (globe and EN), next to the theme button, then Français; same way to come back to English. The choice is remembered on the device.

Why is the "Monthly update" menu in bold, with a red dot? No balance of the current month is entered yet: it reminds you, and goes back to normal as soon as you enter it. An email reminder is also possible (My account, monthly reminder).

Where are my savings goals? Goals menu to follow them; Monthly update, Goals tab, to create and change them (savings goals).

Can I try Patrimeter without creating an account? Yes, if the instance offers the demo: Try the demo on the sign-in page. The account and its fictitious data are deleted after 2 hours or at sign-out (trying without an account).

items.title: Monthly update
items.text: Monthly update menu (Update on a phone), in three tabs: Net worth (the balances of the accounts, described here) and Budget (the amounts of the household budget) for the same month, and Goals (creating and changing your savings goals). This menu, the last one on the right, is always put forward; as long as no balance of the current month is entered, it turns red, with a dot, to remind you. The Net worth part shows all the accounts open that month, on a single screen, one table per level of the pyramid. Enter the balances (English format: 12,345.67), then save the month's balances (Save … balances). Next month can be entered in advance (last arrow, or the calendar); once saved, the Net worth page shows that month.

items.title: Reading the screen
items.text:
Each row shows the account, its status, its balance for the previous month and the field for the month being entered. On a phone, the previous balance moves under the account name.

  • entered (green dot): a balance is already saved for this month.
  • carried over (grey dot, badge): no balance this month; the field is pre-filled with the last known balance, whose month is shown in the badge.
  • no balance: the account has no balance yet.
  • to refine (dashed badge): approximate amount given when the account was created, on the welcome pages. Correct it if needed: saving records it as the month's balance and removes the mention.
  • Loans are marked owed: their amount is the outstanding principal, preceded by "−" and underlined with dots, and it is deducted from the level.

At the top right, a small bar shows how many accounts are entered ("4/8 entered"). Under each table, Level net gives the total of the level; at the bottom, the month's net worth. These totals are worked out again as you type and take into account your share of properties owned with others (real estate).

Under a changed amount, a discreet difference compares it with the previous month ("+€460.00 vs Oct 2026"); for a loan, a lower principal owed is a positive difference. Under the month's net worth, the same difference applies to the whole net worth, worked out again as you type.

An account that has not moved is confirmed in one gesture: the = Oct 2026 button under its field takes the previous month's balance, marks it "entered" and moves to the next account.

A level whose balances are all entered this month is folded: only its name, the word entered and its total stay visible, to leave room for what is left to do. Tap its name to unfold it and correct a balance; it also unfolds by itself when you reach it with the keyboard. Its balances are still saved with the others.

items.title: Entering quickly with the keyboard
items.text:
Key Effect Enter confirms the amount (the account becomes "entered") and moves to the next field, without sending the form Shift + Enter goes back to the previous field Esc restores the suggested amount = takes the previous month's balance (the account becomes "entered") and moves to the next field

These shortcuts, and the reminder about loans, are in the ? help to the right of the legend.

items.title: What is saved
items.text:
• Saving the month (Save … balances) records all the balances shown as the month's balances.
  • An account left empty is not saved: it keeps its last known balance, carried over to the following months. So there is no need to enter, every month, an account that does not move.
  • For a loan, enter the outstanding principal, with or without the "−": 167,612.87 and −167,612.87 mean the same amount.
  • For a property, enter the total value of the property: Patrimeter applies your share.
  • For another month, choose it at the top of the page: to catch up on a forgotten month or correct a past month. As long as no account exists, the update stays on the current month and offers neither another month nor a copy of the balances: only Create an account and Create a property.
  • If the entry changes the status of a savings goal, a message says so at once ("Goal "Down payment": Behind → On track").

items.title: Copying balances from another month
items.text:
To fill in a past year quickly, start from a month already entered: Copy balances from another month, at the top of the monthly update, fills the form with the balances of the chosen month (entered or carried over). The month is picked from the calendar, as at the top of the pages. The copied rows are marked "copied"; correct what has changed, then save the month: nothing is saved before. An account without a balance in the chosen month keeps its usual value. The same box leads to adding an account or a property.

Going back in time. You started Patrimeter in November and want to enter October? Go to October: if no account is open that month yet, the page offers the copy directly, from the current month. Copy the November balances: the accounts opened after October are included too, marked "opening moved back". When you save, their opening date moves to 1 October and their October balances are saved; an account whose field you empty keeps its original opening date. For a property, its initial ownership share also applies to the earlier month, including to its prorated loan. Later changes keep their effective dates.

items.title: My account
items.text:
The My account button (profile icon), at the top right of every page, opens the account menu:

  • My profile: the My account page;
  • AI agents: tokens and applications of the API and the MCP service, if the administrator has enabled them (API and MCP);
  • Documentation: this documentation, in the language of the interface (if the administrator offers it);
  • Sign out.

The My account page is split into tabs, to quickly find what there is to set: all the settings are there (accounts, real estate, budget household and categories, Carbure), and the main menu only keeps Net worth, Budget and Monthly update. Sensitive actions (changing app, new backup codes, new recovery key, signing out the other sessions, creating a token, exporting your data, deleting the account) ask you to confirm your identity: password, valid for 5 minutes.

Tab Sections For Profile Profile, Password, Monthly reminder, Language of the emails, Your data, Delete my account Sign-in address and sign-in methods; changing the password (the current one is asked, your data remains readable); monthly reminder by email; language of the emails; export and import; deleting the account Sign-in and security Second factor, Passkeys (FIDO2) and security keys, Open sessions, Trusted browsers, Sign-in log Changing app, generating new backup codes, new recovery key; adding, renaming or deleting a passkey or a FIDO2 key; open sessions, to sign out one by one or all together; trusted browsers, to remove; successful or refused sign-ins, with the IP address: spot a suspicious attempt Accounts Accounts by level, archived accounts Creating, editing, archiving an account or a loan (accounts and loans) Real estate One table per property Creating a property and its loans, your share (real estate) Tax household and categories Tax household, budget categories and items Adults, children (years of birth), emergency savings target, categories and items (household budget) Carbure Your instance, mappings Linking your Carbure instance and matching its categories with those of the budget (Carbure) AI agents Connect an AI agent, API and applications Addresses of the MCP service and of the API, personal tokens and access granted to applications (API and MCP); tab missing if the API and the MCP are disabled

An email warns you of every security change. If you did not make it, it says what to do: change the password from My account, or, when the change may have shut you out (password changed or reset, authenticator app replaced, account deleted), tell the server administrator.

items.title: Open sessions
items.text:
In the Sign-in and security tab, the Open sessions box lists, like the sign-in log, every device where you are signed in: sign-in date, last activity, IP address and browser; yours is marked this session. A session closes on its own after 30 minutes without activity, and at the latest 12 hours after signing in.

Once your identity is confirmed, Sign out closes another session, and Sign out my other sessions closes them all except yours (the API tokens fall too). The device concerned goes back to the sign-in page at its next request. A device you do not recognise: sign it out, then change your password.

To add or change a passkey or a FIDO2 key, the page reminds you, highlighted, to confirm your identity first in the Second factor box.

items.title: Trusted browsers
items.text:
On the verification code screen, tick Trust this browser for 30 days: on this browser, the next sign-ins only ask for the password (or the passkey), without the code, for 30 days. Never tick it on a shared or public computer.

The Trusted browsers box of the Sign-in and security tab lists them: date added, last use, end of validity, IP address and browser; yours is marked this browser. Once your identity is confirmed, Remove removes one, and Remove all trusted browsers removes them all: the code will be asked for again at the next sign-in. Changing your password or signing out your other sessions also removes them all. The sign-in log records each sign-in without code ("Sign-in without code (trusted browser)").

items.title: Monthly reminder
items.text:
Monthly reminder (Profile tab): tick Receive the reminder and choose the day of the month. On that day, from 9:00 (the instance's time), if no balance of the month is entered, Patrimeter sends you an email with a link to the monthly entry; once a month. The section gives the sender's address: add it to your contacts so that the reminder does not land in spam. It holds no amount: outside your session, the server cannot read your data. With the challenges on, it also gives your entry streak and what entering the month would bring to it ("By entering November 2026, your streak goes up to 3 months: a new star of the “Entry streak” challenge."): only the months entered and the stars earned are used, never an amount. The link at the bottom of the email turns the reminder off without signing in (a page, then a button). The reminder only exists if the instance sends emails.

If mail delivery fails, the reminder remains eligible for the next hourly run while the month still needs an entry.

items.title: Language of the emails
items.text: Language of the emails (Profile tab): Français, English, or That of the interface at the time of sending (the default choice). It applies to all the emails of Patrimeter: monthly reminder, security alerts, forgotten password, deletion of the account.

items.title: Deleting your account
items.text:
Profile tab, Delete my account section: first confirm your identity, type the email address of your account (shown above the field; capital letters and surrounding spaces do not count), then Delete my account and confirm one last time. Another address deletes nothing.

  • Everything is deleted: accounts, balances, shares, properties, budget, link with Carbure, family members, sign-in methods (passkeys, backup codes), tokens and access of AI agents, sign-in log.
  • Nothing can be recovered, not even by the administrator: export your data first if you want to keep it (your data).
  • You are signed out, and an email confirms the deletion. The address can then be used for a new registration.
  • The data you had exported to a family account stays there: that account removes it.

items.title: Forgotten password
items.text:
Forgotten your password? on the sign-in page sends a link (30 minutes). Then:

  • with your recovery key: new password, data kept;
  • with a passkey that unlocks (PRF): sign in with it, then change your password;
  • with neither: access is restored, but the data is lost, after explicit confirmation. Nobody, not even the administrator, can recover it.

items.title: Lost phone
items.text: Sign in with a backup code, then change app in My account. Without a backup code, the administrator can reset your second factor after checking your identity.

items.title: Net worth
items.text:
The Net worth page, first menu and home page, shows the month's net worth and its pyramid. The net worth box also shows your level of the challenges and your number of stars, with a link to them; the Accounts and Real estate buttons, at the top, lead to what it is made of, and Indicators to your own totals (indicators).

Level Examples Main residence Your home, and its mortgage Emergency savings Current account, savings accounts Guaranteed funds Guaranteed funds (fonds euros) of life insurance Equities PEA, securities account, unit-linked funds Real estate Rental properties, SCPI Alternative Crypto-assets, gold and other precious metals, jewellery, watches, works of art, wines, car, motorbike, unusual investments

Each level shows its net value (its assets minus the loans linked to it) and its share of the total. The arrows and the selector change the month. As long as no account exists, the page stays on the current month, the one where you create your first accounts: no arrows and no selector (the same for the monthly update).

From any other month, including next month, the selector lets you return directly to the current month.

Hovering a level of the pyramid, or clicking it, highlights its lines in the other boxes (Breakdown by level, How your investments are split, Since the start of the year): tinted background and a bar on the left, the other levels of the pyramid fade. A click keeps the highlight; a second click, a click elsewhere or Escape removes it. The other way round, hovering a line or reaching it with the keyboard highlights its level in the pyramid.

Calculation rules:

  • the value of an account for a month is its balance for that month, otherwise its last earlier balance (carried over);
  • an account counts from the month it was opened, and up to the month before it was closed.

In a family account, a choice at the top of the page shows the whole family, one member or this account; it also applies to the report and the budget.

items.title: Net worth trends
items.text:
Under the recommendations, Net worth trends gives the change of the net worth over 3, 6 and 12 months up to the month shown (and what that makes per month), next to the change over the same length just before: is your net worth growing faster or slower than before?

From the 20th of the month, if no balance of the current month is entered, the page points it out at the top, with a link to the monthly entry.

items.title: Sharing a report
items.text:
To show your net worth to your family, Share (next to the month selector) opens a report for the month: a card without menus, with the net worth, its change over 1 month and over 1 year, the pyramid, the gross assets and the liabilities. On a phone, it fills the whole screen: a screenshot shows it alone.

  • The report only shows the levels of the pyramid, never the names of your accounts or your banks.
  • Hide amounts only keeps the percentages: the breakdown and the change, without revealing the sums. Show amounts brings them back.
  • Show my stars adds, under the pyramid, your stars and your level of the challenges ("★ 15 stars · level 4: Far-sighted"), on the card and on the picture; never an amount. Offered only for your own net worth, with the challenges on; Hide my stars removes them.
  • The report follows the month chosen on the Net worth page, and the light or dark theme of the screen.
  • Patrimeter publishes and sends nothing: the page stays private to your account, only the picture you share leaves your device.

Below the card, Patrimeter turns it into a picture (a 1080 × 1350 pixel PNG, Instagram's portrait format), in your browser:

  • Share the picture… opens the phone's share sheet (or the computer's, if it has one): choose the app, Instagram, WhatsApp, Mastodon, Signal…
  • Save the picture downloads it.
  • Post on Mastodon, X (Twitter), Facebook, WhatsApp or Instagram: on a phone, the share sheet opens with the picture; on a computer, the picture is saved and the network opens in a new tab, with a short text for Mastodon, X and WhatsApp: add the saved picture to it. For Mastodon, enter your server (for example mastodon.social); the browser remembers it.
  • With amounts, a warning reminds you: posted on a social network, the picture makes them public. Hide amounts before sharing only keeps the percentages.

items.title: How your investments are split
items.text:
Under the pyramid, a table compares the share of each level in your investments with a benchmark: the "balanced" allocation of Avenue des Investisseurs (update of 7 February 2026), which inspired the wealth pyramid.

Level Benchmark Guaranteed funds 45% Equities 25% Real estate 25% Alternative 5% (10% at most)
  • Investments are the sum of these four levels, minus loans. The main residence (base of the pyramid) and emergency savings (about three months of expenses) have no percentage.
  • This is only a guide, not investment advice: the right split depends on your time horizon and your risk appetite.
  • Without positive investments, the table is not shown.

items.title: Since the start of the year
items.text:
Under the source of the benchmark, a second table shows what was put into or taken out of each level of the pyramid since the start of the year, then for the net worth: the net value of the chosen month minus that at the end of December of the previous year (or of January, if your balances start this year). It gives an overview of the savings of the year.

  • Patrimeter only knows balances: the change also includes gains and losses (equities, real estate…) and, for the levels that have a loan, the capital repaid.
  • A rise is shown with a + sign, a fall with a − sign: the meaning does not rely on colour.

items.title: Recommendations
items.text:
To the right of how your investments are split, the Recommendations box reads the month's pyramid together with your budget for the same month.

  • Emergency savings: their amount compared with the budget's monthly expenses (needs and wants, savings excluded), in months of expenses, on a gauge:
    • the track has three zones: less than one month, below the household's target, from the target to twice the target;
    • the bar stops at the number of months covered, the line marks the target (3 months by default, set it in Tax household and categories);
    • a finding comes with the gauge: Alert below one month of expenses, Warning below the target (with the missing amount), Good once the target is reached, Note above twice the target (the surplus could be invested higher up the pyramid).
  • Without a budget for the month, Patrimeter does not know your expenses: the box invites you to enter the budget, and shows an Alert if your emergency savings are empty.
  • Pyramid: the pyramid is built from the base up. A finding points out equities or alternative investments held while emergency savings fall short of their target, a negative level (loans above the value of the assets), and the largest gap with the allocation benchmark, from 15 points. Without any finding: "Nothing to report".

Each finding has a word and an icon, on top of its colour. These are indicative benchmarks, not investment advice.

items.title: Your position among French households
items.text:
Under the details by level, two cards side by side (one under the other on a phone) place your net worth. The left one places your net worth for the month among that of French households: "your net worth is higher than that of about 63% of households", your decile, and a scale from the least to the best off, with the median marked. Benchmarks and source details the thresholds.

  • Reference: Insee, Histoire de vie et Patrimoine survey 2023-2024, household net worth in early 2024 (median: €148,100; top 10%: more than €750,400; top 1%: more than €2,728,900).
  • Between two published thresholds, the position is estimated along a straight line.
  • The comparison is between households: if you only track your own share, and not the wealth of your whole household, your position is underestimated. Insee counts neither durable goods (car, furniture), nor valuables, nor pension rights.
  • The calculation is done on your server: nothing is sent elsewhere.

items.title: Your position among adults worldwide
items.text:
The right card makes the same comparison on a worldwide scale: "your net worth is higher than that of about 83% of adults worldwide", with a scale graduated at the published band thresholds.

  • Reference: UBS, Global Wealth Report 2026, net worth per adult at the end of 2025, in 56 countries that hold more than 92% of global wealth. Under $10,000: 42.1% of adults; under $100,000: 83.2%; under one million: 98.5%; under 5 million: 99.8%.
  • The dollar thresholds are converted into euros at the ECB rate of 31 December 2025 ($1.1750 for €1): $10,000 is €8,511, $100,000 is €85,106, one million is €851,064.
  • The report only publishes these bands: within each of them, the position is estimated (along a straight line under $10,000, according to the logarithm of net worth above that, each band covering a factor of 10).
  • The comparison is between adults, not households: if you track a couple's net worth, your position is overestimated.

items.title: History
items.text: At the very bottom of the Net worth page: how your net worth and each level change over time, as a chart, over the chosen period (12 months, 2 years, 5 years or all), up to the month shown, with the table of monthly values. The period and view buttons (Net total or By level) keep the chosen month and come back to the history. The former /historique address also leads there.
